On the other hand, Vik the witch followed them around for some unknown reason. With the help of Wallace, they went to the Misty Forest in search of Hela's servant Greti. Because Vik and Greti were old acquaintances, Greti agreed to help them, and asked them to go back and wait for news.
Greti soon contacted them, and the three met Town of the Dead's ruler — Hela the Goddess of Death. Hela told them that there was nothing she could do at present. She could only free all the souls for them if they could obtain the tears of the Heartless. They promised to help Hela restore the altar, so Hela provided a clue that pointed to the Heartless's identity. Siren was annoyed by Vik's babbling. He wanted to save his father as soon as possible, and had no time to waste on Vik, but Vik, though ignored, insisted on following Siren around. The three soon found that the altar couldn't be restored due to the existence of the vengeful soul.
When looking into the vengeful soul's sad past, the three unexpectedly discovered a secret opposition group in the Town of the Dead. Its members believed that Hela was the one trapping all the souls, so they were doing whatever they could to disrupt the altar's restoration, which caused Siren a headache. On the other hand, Hela's servant Greti liked to be with humans, and befriended Vik. He helped them secretly, and found Enoch the artifact researcher, who lived in the Misty Forest.
Enoch incited the opposition group, trying to use them to seize Authority over the Nine Worlds — Hela's artifact. He was the one who caused the tragedy of the vengeful soul. Siren and Vik decided to reveal Enoch's true colors, whether it was to help the vengeful soul or to restore the altar. Deep in the Misty Forest, the three found the opposition group's stronghold and revealed Enoch's true colors to the group's leader. They also told him that they were repairing the altar to free the souls, and succeeded in convincing him not to disrupt the restoration any more. The spirits hindering the restoration all left, and the vengeful soul at the altar disappeared. After the altar was restored, Siren, Vik, and the Adventurer went to Hela's palace together, but instead of Hela, waiting there for them was Greti alone...
2831482:
As promised, Hela provided a clue of the Heartless to Siren through Greti, but none of the three could understand the message. On the other hand, Greti covertly told them a secret: At Skellington, there was a gemstone called Sylid. It could summon everyone and everything its holder wanted to see.
However, when the crew arrived at Skellington, they found Glott of Sloth, another of Hela's servants, waiting for them, who launched fierce attacks on them without warning.
After escaping the Sloth Beast's pursuit, the crew decided to ask a local resident — Duke Pumpkin for Sylid's whereabouts. Actually, Hela's treasury where Sylid was kept was right in a certain forbidden tomb chamber in Skellington.
Miss Carly the top-class tailor made them Hela's boots that allowed them to step into the forbidden area, and they sneaked in by disguising as Whispers.
Siren, Vik, and the Adventurer managed to overcome various challenges the tomb chamber threw at them, and finally reached Sylid, the gemstone containing power of the Death, but before they could summon the Heartless, Vik wished for delicious food! The gemstone granted the wish and shattered in a burst of green light, rendering all the efforts so far futile. A furious Siren vented to Vik and asked her to get out. Hurt by Siren's words and behaviors, Vik left the team sadly. Faced with this gloomy situation, everyone's heart sank into an unprecedented abyss of despair. Just then, Glott of Sloth appeared and announced that Siren and the Adventurer had passed all of Hela's tests in Skellington, and she would give them the second clue about the Heartless once they restored the Altar of Life leading to Hela's palace. Was this a sign of dawn that could end the night of despair, or a fatal trap with dangerous undertows? And what will become of the divided Niflheim team of three?
2831483:
Wallace helped the Adventurer and Siren figure out that Hela's second clue was pointing at Niflheim 66 — Vik's residence. Talked around by the Adventurer, Siren put his anger against Vik down temporarily, and decided to go talk to Vik, partly to apologize, and partly to decode the second clue. To make up for the rude attitude before, Siren and the Adventurer decided to please Vik with desserts. It was right during the celebration of the Hela Festival, so Siren and the Adventurer redeemed candies from ghosts at Niflheim, and went to Vik's house at No. 66 with them.
To their surprise, Vik wasn't in. Instead, there was a note full of regret, in which she apologized to Siren and told him that she was going to Hela's chamber to find another gemstone. Foreseeing the danger Vik might put herself in, Siren and the Adventurer went to Skellington at once, and found Vik being attacked by Poisonous Rattan. Although the battle helped Siren and Vik reconcile, Siren was accidentally poisoned. Vik brought Siren back to her house and made an antidote with the help of the Adventurer.
The crew thought that the pipe organ in the house might give them a hint to decode the second clue, so they played it, and Vik's friend Gordon showed up all of a sudden. Gordon said that he could take Siren to a special place, but he must eat food of the Town of the Dead to enter the state of suspended animation. Siren and the Adventurer found Wallace and swallowed the weird-tasting meal of the dead grudgingly. However, it was a trap of Gordon, who was ordered by Hela to put Siren and the Adventurer to eternal suspended animation. They were only saved from the crisis when Vik got them an antidote.
The crew went to Gordon again to confront him, but accidentally entered Hela's dream during the fight. Although they got to know Hela's past and her beloved dog Garm, the clue decoding stuck again due to Vik's suddenly worsened health. The helpless crew then met Hela's servant Reva, who told them that Lady Hela had prepared a trial for them, and asked them to go to Greti and Glott.
Guided by Greti and Glott, the crew entered the Eljudnir Palace, defeated Greed and Moon Shadow Illusion, and used the bone Reva gave them to handle Garm the giant bloodstained dog. After that, they finally met Hela herself, and the showdown started. At last, the defeated Hela revealed the truth — Vik was Hela's heart, and the Heartless referred to Hela the Goddess of Death herself. The adventure so far had created a certain bond between Siren and Vik. Faced with Vik's gravely question, Siren had no choice but to make a hard decision...
2831484:
Contact with the team of six gone to Lighthalzen was completely lost. Shortly after that, there was a great fire at Rekenber Co., which worried Commander Healueman profoundly. He requested the Adventurer to do the investigation. On a plain near Lighthalzen, he met the spirit of a girl, who tried to dissuade him from venturing further, because the road ahead was extremely dangerous. However, the Adventurer didn't back down. Soon, he had a formal meeting with Wesley, who had come to assist him. Shouldering Wesley's expectation and bearing his exhortations in mind, the Adventurer continued to pursue the truth...
After the Adventurer arrived in Lighthalzen, he ran into Hollgrehenn, who was here looking for his master Hayward. Just when the two wondered what to do next, a Peco Peco showed up and brought them hope — it was Lili, Seyren's mount! Following Lili, the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn found an unconscious Magaleta. After waking her, the crew  reviewed all the clues they had, and came up with an unexpected destination: Rekenber Co....
Confused, they made it past the guards and reached Rekenber's underground laboratory, where they finally met Seyren. However, before they could rejoice at the reunion, Seyren revealed the cruel reality: Rekenber was experimenting on humans here, and those who accompanied him here had probably become victims! Not willing to believe this, Hollgrehenn set out to look for Hayward alone. The Adventurer and the others followed him, but when they found Hayward, the latter had already lost his mind and knocked Hollgrehenn out... Everyone was shocked. To find out what drove Hayward crazy, they started to investigate this weird laboratory.
As the investigation proceeded, they met countless mutated creatures, as well as mutated humans. Seyren noticed that the condition of those humans was similar to that of Hayward. They struggled for more clues, and finally discovered the true nature of the experimental subjects: They would gradually lose their conscious and duplicate themselves until they turned into soulless golems that wander this dungeon forever. The cause of the mutation turned out to be a shard of an artificial Yimir heart!
Faced with the laboratory's sinful conducts, and the fact that his companions had probably become victims, Seyren was indignant. He came to the resolution to save all the mutated people. During the investigation, the Adventurer's crew met the ghost of a firefighter. The sudden fire at the laboratory was also related to Rekenber's evildoings. To gather more clues, the crew decided to split up and go on exploring this mysterious and weird place...
2831486:
The reunited six-member team decided to work together to uncover Rekenber Co.'s conspiracy. They advanced into the depths of the laboratory, only to discover that the experimental subjects were beyond saving. Deeven and the others made an important decision: they were willing to sacrifice themselves for Seyren and Margaretha to escape with the data. Seyren adamantly refused Deeven's proposal, insisting that the six-member team stick together. At that moment, Cenia appeared and attacked KateLina. Allemes quickly shielded KateLina, and they realized that Cenia's eyes had turned blood-red and she had become a puppet of Bouleseph.

After being attacked by Cenia, Allemes closed his eyes forever. The remaining five members, despite their pain, vowed to expose Rekenber's conspiracy to the world. However, at this time, Margaretha fell into a dream again. The adventurer and Deeven, along with Hayward, went to Rekenber Research Room to obtain evening primrose to heal Margaretha. Unexpectedly, Bouleseph had set an ambush, and Hayward sacrificed himself to protect the evening primrose. Deeven tearfully returned with the evening primrose. Surprisingly, in Magaleta's Dream, they saw her bargaining with Bouleseph: sacrificing four companions in exchange for Seyren and her freedom.

Seyren, knowing the truth, decided to separate from Margaretha, and the remaining three continued their investigation into the depths of the institute. A videotape they found in the lab revealed the reason for the maker's loss of control: KateLina's madness caused a massive explosion in the lab, causing the Artificial Yimir Heart Maker to rise into the air. To reach the lab, the adventurer suggested using an airship.

After obtaining the airship key, they found out that the fuel for the airship was the Artificial Yimir Heart. To obtain the fuel, they headed to the energy warehouse, only to have a crazed XueYi detonate and destroy the warehouse to stop them. In the critical moment, Deeven sacrificed himself, using his blood infused with the power of the Artificial Yimir Heart to power the airship. Bouleseph had anticipated their appearance in the air lab and sent out thought forms of Allemes and the others, causing the six-member team to turn on each other. Not only that, he even made Cenia the guardian of the Artificial Yimir Heart to hinder the adventurers. Just as they were about to lose hope, Siren's appearance awakened Cenia's rationality, and she chose to self-destruct along with Bouleseph. However, the Artificial Yimir Heart Maker still existed, and Margaretha decided to stay behind and destroy it to atone for her sins. At this moment, Seyren held Margaretha's hand, willing to face this challenge together. The adventurer left the lab with the mission of exposing the truth, bringing Rekenber Co.'s conspiracy into the light.
2831487:
A group of unexpected visitors arrived at the Louen Kingdom — envoys from the Arunafeltz States. The envoys invited outstanding adventurers of the Louen Kingdom to their pope's coronation to ease the tension between the two countries. The Adventurer headed to Rachel, capital of Arunafeltz, to honor the task.
After arriving at Rachel, the Adventurer met the crowned prince and princess — boy-girl twins Lucas and Shatira. The two welcomed the Adventurer, a guest from Louen, warmly, and offered to show him around Rachel.
However, on the day of the coronation and on his way to an audience with Mother Cesia, the Adventurer witnessed her being killed by her son Lucas, and Lucas declared that he would annex Louen.
To protect the Louen Kingdom and help Shatira, the Adventurer tracked Lucas and looked into his conspiracy. He saw Lucas collude with rebellious acolytes, and took pictures as proofs.
2831488:
Shatira called back High Priest Jed of Rachel, who was on a retreat. She and the Adventurer told him about Lucas's conducts. For the future of Rachel, Jed decided to reveal the truth to all followers in Rachel.
Shatira implored all the followers to forgive her brother, offering to give her own life in return. Moved by Shatira's attitude, the followers elected her Pope of Rachel.
The Adventurer thought this concluded the incident, but Shatira then ordered in the name of the goddess that the Adventurer be killed. Just then, Niloyan, Cesia's personal maid, took the Adventurer to safety.
To find out Shatira's true purpose, the Adventurer and Niloyan went to the Holy Temple again, but it was actually Shatira's trap. The murderer Adventurer saw was Shatira in disguise, and the real Lucas had been imprisoned by Shatira in an ice cave.
Since Shatira had inherited the power of Yimir's heart in the scepter, the Adventurer was outpowered, and also locked up in the ice cave, where he managed to tackle all the obstructions and save Lucas.
Then, the Adventurer discovered the secrets hidden in the ice cave: Cesia had always loved Lucas and neglected Shatira. She even used Shatira's blood to heal Lucas. Having found out what his sister went through, Lucas blamed himself and decided to go back to Rachel and put an end to the whole matter.
Due to the bond between twins, Shatira was aware of Lucas being rescued, and had already prepared for it in Rachel. She told Lucas that their mother did all of this because of an oracle.
Years of imprisonment and torture had driven Shatira crazy. She wanted to offer Lucas to the goddess's statue and destroy everything, but the Adventurer and Lucas acted in sync and stopped Shatira together.
Just then, Hand of Goddess, who had been assisting Shatira covertly, appeared in an attempt to kill Shatira the loser. Lucas shielded his sister with his own body, wishing that she would be the survivor this time, because he owed her a debt...
Seeing her twin brother lying in a puddle of blood, Shatira made a decision. She sacrificed herself to revive Lucas with the power of Yimir's heart.
2831489:
Preparation of the ritual was finished, and Elly the chief priest began the spirit-summoning ritual. Everyone thought it was going to be a success, but the light of the divine tree faded, and the ritual failed.
Elly said that she sensed the divine tree's will: it didn't want to wake up. When the Adventurer was examining the divine tree, he heard the sound of flute from the previous day again. The Adventurer told Romani about the flute. Romani didn't hear it, but he agreed that they might wake the divine tree with a flute.
Therefore, the Adventurer started to seek the source of the flute sound alone, and found the blind Maple. After a chat, Maple agreed to wake the divine tree for the Adventurer, but since he was quite feeble at the moment, he needed some rest first. The two made a deal to go to the divine tree on the next day.
When the Adventurer took Maple to the divine tree, Maple realized that he could sense light. The divine tree seed really reacted to his flute performance. Romani expressed his gratitude, but the Adventurer found that he couldn't see Maple.
Because of this, Maple started to question his own identity. The Adventurer thus took Maple to Elly for an answer. Unable to withstand the pain of spirit check, Maple fell into a coma, while Elly told the Adventurer sadly that Maple was a fading spirit.
To save Maple, the Adventurer started looking for Soul Binding Grass, during which he was threatened by a spooky, hoarse voice. Its owner born great malice against both the divine tree and Maple.
The Soul Binding Grass the Adventurer gathered finally cured Maple. He calmly accepted the fact that he had died, yet he still hoped to retrieve his memories. Since Maple seemed to have a connection with the divine tree, the Adventurer decided to help him.
2831490:
The Adventurer was looking for clues to Maple's memories at the Wasteland when he was attacked by a wraith. The wraith knew Maple, and expressed his hatred for Luoyang.
After a fierce battle, the wraith retreated. The Adventurer tracked his magic and found him conspiring with a mysterious woman to destroy Luoyang's barrier. They were also responsible for monster mutations and the attack on the divine tree. Unfortunately, the Adventurer was discovered when eavesdropping. The mysterious woman, who turned out to be Bijou, attacked him with the wraith. Good thing Maple appeared in time and fought alongside the Adventurer.
Seeing Maple, the wraith was emotionally compromised and ran away, while Bijou attacked Maple when the Adventurer wasn't watching before she escaped. The Adventurer was worried about Maple's injury, but Maple said he was fine and only needed some rest. However, something seemed to have happened to the divine tree, so he asked the Adventurer to check it out.
The Adventurer went back to the divine tree, and found it a bit taller. When the Adventurer went to Maple again, Maple said that he had regained part of his sight, and he had also retrieved some memory after meeting the wraith. Maple requested the Adventurer to find a mysterious place. After some research, the Adventurer found that the place on Maple's mind was the Moonlight Grotto.
The Adventurer entered the Moonlight Grotto to explore it, and found a Memory Box in the crystal tree. Opening the Memory Box, the Adventurer found a scroll painting and a Bosom Friend Bird. The bird told him that the scroll painting belonged to Gunn, and described what happened in the past.
Suddenly, flames burst out in the grotto — the wraith had appeared, trying to sneak attack the Adventurer. Just then, power came out of the scroll painting, protecting the Adventurer and removing the wraith's disguise. The Adventurer was amazed to see that the wraith looked exactly the same as Maple!
His real appearance revealed, the wraith left madly. Although the Adventurer managed to escape the fire, he had many doubts that needed to be solved.
The Adventurer found Maple near the divine tree and told him about what happened in the Moonlight Grotto. Laying his hands on the scroll painting, Maple seemed to remember everything. His flute brought another growth spurt to the divine tree, turning it into a giant tree. Then, Maple bade the Adventurer goodbye and went off.
Now that the divine tree had grown up, the Adventurer found Fa Hai, and told him what happened lately. Fa Hai took the scroll painting and told the Adventurer about Maple's background and events that happened in Luoyang a hundred years ago. During the war that year, Ulo the leader of Venom Fang died, rendering the barrier unable to be activated. To protect Luoyang, Gunn the leader of Vana had to turn into a giant dragon himself and build a barrier with his own body.
Fa Hai also mentioned the wraith, who looked exactly the same as Ulo. He was worried that the wraith and his backers might cause more trouble in the Wasteland. Therefore, he asked the Adventurer to return to the Wasteland. He also gave the Adventurer an invisibility scroll to protect him from incoming danger.
2831491:
The adventurer came to Wasteland again to investigate the anomaly, only to find that Feng was trapped by the evil spirit and Bijou. The adventurer was about to rescue Feng, but did not expect that this was a trap set by Bijou and the evil spirit. The two teamed up to trap the adventurer in an illusion, and it seemed that there was another conspiracy.

When the adventurer left the illusion, Wasteland had already fallen into chaos, and monsters were rampant everywhere. The adventurer rescued Romanine and other Wasteland patrol members, and learned the whereabouts of the evil spirit from them, so he chased after Moonlight Grotto.

However, the entrance of the cave was sealed by a barrier, and the adventurer could not enter. Wasteland's sacrifice, Elly, appeared in time, saying that she could break the barrier and asked the adventurer to wait patiently.

Elly unlocked the seal of the cave, the adventurer entered, and found that the evil spirit set up a formation to distort the memory box and absorb evil power from it.

After the adventurer destroyed the formation, the evil spirit woke up in a rage. He accused Gunn of betraying him and vowed to destroy Luoyang. Bijou also sent puppets to disturb the adventurer, asking the evil spirit to take the memory box away and destroy the divine tree.

After defeating Bijou's Puppet, the adventurer chased the evil spirit and finally defeated it in front of the divine tree, but the evil spirit was unwilling to disappear. At this moment, Feng— or rather Ulo, reappeared. He purified the resentment from the evil spirit and absorbed the lost half of its body.

The crisis in Wasteland was resolved, but the adventurer also had to say goodbye to Ulo: Due to the use of power of the divine tree, Ulo would merge with the tree and fall into a long sleep. Ulo comforted the lost adventurer and asked the new friend to continue enjoying the red maple of Wasteland on his behalf...
2831492:
The adventurer learned that the appearance of the demonic energy was due to Bijou casting a curse. During the pursuit of Bijou, the adventurer was deceived by Bijou's trickery, ambushed, and severely injured. In the moment of danger, a young man of the Fana tribe appeared and saved the adventurer. The young man advised the adventurer to leave Maple Leaf Faramita quickly and then left.

The adventurer was very confused, and under Yzma's guidance, they met Ulo and the Fana youth who had just saved them. It turned out that this young man of the Fana tribe was the dragon Gunn. When Gunn saw the adventurer, he once again turned and left. Ulo apologized to the adventurer on Gunn's behalf. The adventurer told Ulo that Gunn had saved them, and Ulo handed the adventurer a compass that could track Gunn's whereabouts.

The adventurer sensed from Gunn's words and actions that Gunn seemed to know their origin and decided to use the compass to find Gunn and get to the bottom of things. During the search, the adventurer accidentally discovered Yzma meeting with Bijou. Bijou tried to manipulate Yzma through her love for Ulo to obey him, but the adventurer immediately intervened. Bijou summoned demons to delay the adventurer and escaped the scene. Gunn appeared again, telling the adventurer that they could find the truth using the compass.

Through great effort, the adventurer found Gunn's notes in Frost Domain and learned that Maple Leaf Faramita was not the true Wasteland from a thousand years ago but only a dreamscape of Gunn's. Gunn revealed the events of the past to the adventurer. At this moment, the entire dreamscape shook violently, and Gunn sent the adventurer away from Maple Leaf Faramita.
2831493:
The glowing fountain in Prontera attracted many Citizens, and the knowledgeable scholars recognized the golden light as the messenger of the Goddess of Fate. The goddess from the divine realm brought prophecies about the future, and the young savior would blow the wind of fate to save this precarious world. The messenger of fate guided the ignorant adventurers through time and space to the giant branches of Yggdrasil Hill. At the top of the tree, within the distant floating clouds, there shone a pair of azure eyes…

At the edge of the divine realm far from Asgard, in the dim area behind the starlight, there was an ancient city. The river from the edge of the sky flowed down, enveloping the continuous maple trees and the faintly visible white houses under the shade. The water flowed into the lake in the city, disturbing the calm lake, causing clusters of lanterns on the lake surface to wobble, and the red maple leaves on the water surface to flow with the waves. This city, surrounded by maple trees and flowing water, was known to the world as the Dragon City. It also had a more romantic name, Luoyang.

Young Xu Xian was the lord of Luoyang, a romantic and compassionate man with a kind heart. Along with Fa Hai, Xu Xian had been diligently managing Luoyang, fulfilling his responsibilities as the lord of the city. He thought he would live a peaceful life like the clear water of Luoyang. All that changed when he met a memorable Naga at the flower street lantern festival, among the fireworks and swimming dragons – Lady White.

Xu Xian fell in love with this girl, who was cold yet gentle on the outside. Xu Xian put aside his identity as the city lord, disguised himself as an ordinary citizen named Ping'an, and cleverly helped Lady White become the Oiran of Luoyang!

However, it seemed that Lady White didn't care about becoming Oiran, and she had other purposes in mind. She used Xu Xian to help her complete the Oiran trials step by step. Obtaining pure water from Silverfish Lake, using the water to purify the monsters in Sunset Beach, everything was developing according to Lady White's plan. But she didn't expect that she would slowly develop feelings for Ping'an, Xu Xian's pseudonym, during their time together. Finally, with Xu Xian's help, Lady White was successfully elected as the Oiran.
2831494:
At a lantern festival in Luoyang, there were oiran dancing. Lady White was dancing on a gorgeous Kongming lantern. Xu Xian looked at her from the palace in the distance. Only when Lady White saw Xu Xian having a friendly conversation with Fa Hai did she find out that this Vana man that had been helping her was one of her enemies. Her heart aching with anger, Lady White sank the lantern she was dancing on into the Whitebait Lake and disappeared.
A thousand years ago, Luoyang wasn't as peaceful as it was then. Morroc and his demon army brought flames of conflicts to the whole world, and that was when the Twilight of the Gods began. Luoyang was not left untouched. Countless demons entered Luoyang via the Rainbow Bridge, forcing the tribes of Vana and Venom Fang into a prolonged war to protect their home. At that time, Fa Hai was still a child. His foster father Gunn was a hero of the era. Enjoying the same status as Gunn the leader of Vana was Ulo, the leader of Venom Fang. He was also an ancient deity created by Yimir. Ulo was gentle and considerate. He adopted a girl who had lost her parents. This girl, fortunate and unfortunate at the same time, was Lady White. Wars are merciless, and fates are cruel. They always rob the world of its beautiful things. A hard battle took Lady White's new family from her… Ulo died among the maple leaves at Luoyang… Meanwhile, Gunn transformed into a giant dragon and rid Luoyang of darkness. He became a god that residents of Luoyang would worship forever. Lady White couldn't understand why Gunn could live and enjoy everyone's worship while her father died miserably on the battlefield… So she came up with a crazy idea… Subordinates of darkness were watching the miserable girl secretly, and guiding her into an abyss of no return… Lady White wasn't supposed to enter the Whitebait Lake, but she got the permission to go to the lake bottom by becoming an oiran. She opened the time rift there in front of Xu Xian and Fa Hai, letting in numerous monsters previously kept out of Luoyang by a barrier, before she disappeared from everyone's view. Because of the rift at the lake bottom, more and more demons were entering Luoyang, putting the city at risk. To fix the giant rift, Fa Hai and the Adventurer ventured into a domain out of the worldline to gather Power of Secret Source, and they found the unconscious Lady White there.
Although they now had Power of Secret Source, to repair the rift, divine power was also needed. Gunn the giant dragon, who was already quite weak, offered all his power and fell into eternal sleep.
Fa Hai was upset, as his father, who he looked up to, sacrificed himself for Luoyang once again.
When Lady White found out about Gunn's sacrifice, she started to doubt whether her revenge was the right choice, but the culprits behind her didn't give her time to repent. They forced Lady White to fulfill her mission, and came into conflict with her when she resisted. Meanwhile, citizens of Luoyang voluntarily gathered beside the Cloud Edge to visit the giant dragon, who would never wake up again… During the memorial service, Lady White stepped forward and claimed that she had a shard of Yimir's heart, which could wake Gunn.
Although Fa Hai doubted her words, he wanted to wake his father so much that he chose to believe her. At the time promised, Lady White took the shard to Cloud Edge and used it to wake Gunn in front of the watchful royal guards. The ritual failed, and Lady White, performer of the ritual, launched an attack against Fa Hai and the royal guards instead. Bijou, a subordinate of Himmelmez, helped Lady White tear Luoyang's time and space barrier again. The two injured Xu Xian, who was protecting Gunn, and escaped Luoyang when Fa Hai wasn't watching.
2831495:
Fa Hai analyzed the whole incident, and noticed something unusual about the Flower Building. The Adventurer and Fa Hai returned to the Flower Building to investigate it. The Flower Building looked as busy as usual. However, Fa Hai found "Lady Verdant" suspicious, and used magic to remove the dancers' disguises. It turned out that the dancers were actually monsters, and the Flower Building was already occupied by them. The real Lady Verdant and dancers were nowhere to be found. The Adventurer and Fa Hai searched the entire Flower Building and finally found Lady Verdant and Lady White in a remote room. It turned out that even the Lady White at Cloud Edge was Himmelmez in disguise.
After being untied, Lady White went to the lake bottom to visit the injured Xu Xian. Her heart was filled with regret when she was told that Himmelmez stabbed Xu Xian while pretending to be her. Lady White told the Adventurer about how Himmelmez incited her to take revenge a thousand years ago. She finally realized that Himmelmez had always been using her as a tool.
Now back to her senses, Lady White went with Fa Hai the commander of the royal guards and the young Adventurer to the seafloor of the Sunset Beach to get medicine for Xu Xian from Himmelmez. To their surprise, Himmelmez handed the medicine over right away.
2831496:
The falling of Rainbow Bridge shards aroused uneasiness in humans on the Midgards continent. No one knew what was going on in that god's domain out of humans' reach. But the sudden appearance of Jörmungandr the Serpent of World suggested that the Adventurer, Wind of Fate, was the cause of everything.
The Adventurer followed Jörmungandr's order to Lester Lighthouse. By the shore there, the sea was illuminated by the moon, and the waves were beating against the Moon Array on the shore. Influenced by the array, the Adventurer couldn't help but touch it, and a memory flowed into his head — a memory that belonged to himself, but was lost...
Jörmungandr created Amastarsia, a flower of the stars, out of the power of Yimir's heart, and tore open a passage to the moon at the Lester Lighthouse, forming a Moon Array. Following the order of her father, Mimir the giant of wisdom, Skuld the Norn transformed into a Fate Messenger and guided the Adventurer through the Moon Array to the lonely and cold moon to help Jörmungandr save his elder brother Fenrir.
However, Fenrir the wolf's voice was heard telling Jörmungandr to mind his own business and leave. Jörmungandr ignored Fenrir's warning and burst into the temple.
Jörmungandr finally found Fenrir chained up in the main hall of the temple. However, the frail Fenrir insisted on declining Jörmungandr's help, claiming that it was his fate. Jörmungandr soon noticed that Fenrir was not alone. He was with Odin the supreme god, who had long been missing ever since Ragnarok! And Fenrir was transferring his power via the chains to the unconscious Odin. Jörmungandr couldn't understand why Fenrir was protecting Odin, since Odin was the cause of their sufferings. Enraged, Jörmungandr destroyed the chains on Fenrir by force, and attacked Odin.
Fenrir blocked Jörmungandr's attack for Odin, and confronted the angry Jörmungandr. Fenrir was surprised at how strong his younger brother had become, but he was still suppressing Jörmungandr with his power. Just then, the moon started to shake violently. Mimir the giant of wisdom revealed his massive body and smashed the Rainbow Bridge — the passage leading to Valhalla — with a punch. The impact shook the moon as well, throwing Jörmungandr and Fenrir off balance. Rocks rained from top of the temple. Fenrir covered Jörmungandr with his own body, so that he wouldn't be hit by the stones.
Yggdrasil trembled severely. The Rainbow Bridge connecting to Valhalla was destroyed, and the sleeping Odin was woken by the happening. That was when the Adventurer was hit by rocks and fainted, losing this part of his memory.
After touching the Moon Array, the Adventurer retrieved his memory about the Rainbow Bridge shattering. He went to the moon via the Moon Array once again, trying to check on Jörmungandr and the rest.
Fenrir and Jörmungandr were still in Odin's temple. Although Odin had woken up, he still needed rest since his power hadn't completely restored. Fenrir told Jörmungandr and the Adventurer what he knew, and questioned whether Odin really did anything cruel to them during the Ragnarok. He thought that there was a real culprit manipulating everything behind the screen. Although Jörmungandr was not convinced, he promised Fenrir not to act recklessly until truth was revealed.
The cogs of fate had started turning. Whether the Adventurer chose to follow fate or break free from it, his choice would be tested by time...
2831497:
In Prontera, a strange old man blocked the way of adventurers. After talking with him, the adventurer discovered that this person was Morgan. It turned out that he had been looking for the uninvited guest who stole An Yimir's Heart Shards - the mysterious female magician Sara Alin. This time Morgan came to ask the adventurer for help in tracking her down. The two of them followed the trail to Amatsu and finally met Sara Alin in front of Guardian Sakura. However, Sara did not take them seriously. After touching the branches and leaves of Guardian Sakura, she disappeared into a mysterious light. As the adventurer and Morgan stared at each other, a white bird appeared. The adventurer rode it to the passage in the cherry blossoms and confronted Sara Alin directly. Faced with the adventurer's relentless pursuit, Sara Alin became increasingly impatient. In order to get rid of the chase, she even directly detonated the passage. The explosion caused a huge shockwave that completely knocked the adventurer out.

When the adventurer woke up, they found themselves in the floating elf kingdom - the Brilliant Realm. Under the guidance of the snow-winged bird, they encountered the innocent and beautiful elf girl Hetty and a mysterious and indifferent elf boy. In order to track down Sara Alin, the adventurer went to the center of the Brilliant Realm, the Elf City Eclage. Then they learned that the goddess Freya, symbolizing beauty and compassion, was healing her wounds here. And Sara Alin was Freya's Saint! In order to get back An Yimir's Heart Shards, the adventurer decided to find Sara and ask for an explanation. The Great Sage Claire told him that in order to see the Saint, he needed the help of the Dawn Holy Maiden. However, the adventurer unexpectedly discovered that the floating elf's Holy Maiden was Hetty. After understanding the adventurer's purpose, Hetty gladly took him to visit Freya. When Freya heard of the sins committed by her Saints and that she was betrayed by her subordinates, she was in great pain. In front of the adventurer, she judged the invaders of the human continent, Arcana, and ordered Sara Alin to return the fragments of Yimir's Heart. During the trial, the adventurer found out that the Saints did all this to repair the destroyed Rainbow Bridge. After retrieving An Yimir's Heart Shards, everything seemed to have settled, and the adventurer appreciated the goddess's fairness. As they were parting, Freya asked the adventurer to help the floating elves repair the Rainbow Bridge. Then, Hetty made the same request and hoped to meet at the Wishing Square after nightfall. However, not long after, the mysterious boy encountered earlier suddenly appeared. He warned the adventurer not to repair the Rainbow Bridge and issued an invitation to meet in the Time Garden in the evening. Unknowingly, night was about to fall. Whether to go to the Wishing Square or the Time Garden, the adventurer fell into deep thought.
2831498:
When the night fell, the Adventurer recalled his promise with Hetty, so he went to the Prayer Plaza as promised. Hetty was glad to know that the Adventurer would like to help repair the Rainbow Bridge. She told the player that he needed to go to the magic array at the sea of clouds to know the current state of the Rainbow Bridge.
To sneak into the Sea of Azure Clouds, Hetty and the Adventurer made a transformation potion together. However, they got the recipe wrong, and Hetty turned into a Mimmy Monster after drinking it! Just then, an elf who called himself Philly stopped them. He seemed to be the Aurora Wings' leader, and was trying to prevent the suspicious visitors from entering the sea of clouds. Just as the Adventurer was wondering what to do, High Priest Zanubia appeared.
Zanubia removed Hetty's disguise with ease, and told the two that there wasn't enough magic to restore the magic array and a Snow Winged Bird's feather was needed to stabilize the array. Therefore, the Adventurer and Hetty headed to Floating Star Rock to get the feather. During the process, the Adventurer had another fight with Philly, before he found out that Philly was Hetty's elder brother. Their misunderstanding was worsening, but luckily, Hetty arrived in time to fix it. Since the Adventurer managed to get the feather, he returned to the sea of clouds with Hetty.
Back at the Sea of Azure Clouds, Zanubia was impressed by their teamwork and bond, but a moment later, when they restored the magic array, there was a violent quake. Following an explosion and some white smoke, a mysterious elf and his army of little fairies burst into the sea of clouds! To the Adventurer's surprise, he was Brandeis, the silver haired youth he met before. The situation in the sea of clouds immediately turned chaotic. The pixies and little fairies were eager to fight, as the Adventurer and Hetty confronted Brandeis.
At Zanubia's order, the pixies launched their attacks at the little fairies. They were on even terms when a weird purple fog of magic suddenly took shape. The thick fog had just shrouded the whole sea of clouds when something else unexpected happened — Philly, who was fighting the little fairies, fell to the ground unconscious, and the pixies also passed out one by one in the purple fog! Seeing this, all beings present were shocked and began to panic. Zanubia suspected that Brandeis caused this. The latter argued in vain before leaving with the remaining little fairies in a hurry.
Her brother Philly and people all unconscious, Hetty was left in sorrow. She decided to carry out the duty of a saintess and find out the truth. However, that was but the tip of the conspiracy concerning pixies and the Rainbow Bridge...
An unknown sleeping disease suddenly struck the entire Eclage. To save her people, Hetty overused her magic and was dying. Seeing that Hetty had fainted again, the Adventurer was deeply distressed. Just then, Zanubia appeared and saved Hetty. She told the two that to bring the spreading disease under control, they needed to go to the Time Garden and destroy a Manna Crystal there. When the two destroyed the crystal successfully, a mysterious power drew them into the inmost part of the garden, where they saw a giant monster. He was actually Mimir, the long-missing giant of wisdom!
Hetty fainted again — meeting Mimir seemed to have caused memory disorders in her. Mimir, on the other hand, solemnly told the Adventurer a prophecy: "The pure dawn and star of night will find the lost treasure in the wind to restore the brilliance of the rainbow." Hetty was the dawn in the prophecy, and all the happenings were related to the Rainbow Bridge. After Mimir finished, a purple fog gradually veiled the Time Garden, and Mimir fell into sleep.
Before they could notice, the Adventurer and Hetty were back in Eclage, and Hetty could no longer recall meeting Mimir. Nevertheless, there was a piece of good news: After the Manna Crystal was destroyed, the sleeping patients were waking! However, the Adventurer and Hetty weren't aware that the tragedy was just beginning...
When the Adventurer met Hetty again, she told him that the sleeping disease plaguing the pixies was not relieved. Although the pixies had woken up, they were deprived of their consciousness and daydreaming like some walking corpses. That was true for Hetty's brother Philly too. The situation added to the anxiety of the already-exhausted Hetty. After analyzing the situation, the Adventurer realized that the sleeping disease only changed after they destroyed the Manna Crystal, and it was Zanubia the high priest who ordered them to do so.
Not able to reach Zanubia, Hetty and the Adventurer planned to go to the Time Garden and ask Mimir about the truth. However, before they could get any answer, they were taken out of the garden by some purple butterflies that popped up from nowhere. They then found themselves at the Birthplace of God, in front of Goddess Freya.
After a conversation with the goddess, the Adventurer and Hetty finally realized that destroying the Manna Crystal and worsening the sleeping disease were all part of Goddess Freya's plan. She allowed the health of pixies to deteriorate and did nothing to prevent their death. The two were enraged, but the goddess looked quite pleased. She killed Philly in front of Hetty, plunging Hetty's mind into darkness.
With the help of Claire the great sage, the Adventurer restored Hetty to her original mental state. Claire told the two that the goddess was the culprit and had a grand evil scheme. To prevent further tragedies, they had to find the treasure in the prophecy. Having said this, Claire died because of the goddess's curse.
The deaths of her brother and her teacher hit Hetty hard. She was no longer the naive saintess. Shouldering hatred and responsibilities, she decided to abandon her past faith and resist the goddess, her biggest idol in the past...
When searching for Hetty, the Adventurer was attacked by the mysterious man in black and nearly killed. He found Hetty at the Floating Star Rock, hiding in a barrier. It turned out that she was avoiding the goddess's surveillance. The Adventurer was then convinced that the man in black who attacked him was also sent by the goddess. The two had a talk and decided to take action now and find the treasure before the goddess.
It seemed that the magic of the Sun on Hetty somehow resonated with the treasure. After a long search, they finally found the treasure at the Mercury Palace — a Ring of Truth with an imprint of the Sun. The two touched the ring and travelled back in time. There, they saw a shocking sight: Freya inflicting a soul curse on the great sage, and having Zanubia extract power from the pixies to restore the Rainbow Bridge. Hetty finally comprehended that the sleeping disease was a result of the pixies' life being extracted, as part of the goddess's plan. She did all of this to repair the Rainbow Bridge and return to God's Domain, where she was going to execute an even more horrible plan...
Returning from the memories in the ring, the Adventurer and Hetty met the long-ambushing Zanubia, who was after the treasure. The two were no match of Zanubia at her full strength. They were going to lose when Hetty created a barrier. She entrusted the Adventurer with the Ring of Truth, and requested him to find the other treasure and thwart Freya's scheme. Then, Hetty sent the Adventurer to safety while she faced Zanubia alone...
2831499:
When the night fell, the Adventurer decided to go to the Time Garden as promised. At the entrance, a strange Star Flower appeared. It claimed to be the silver haired youth himself, but would only assume its true form if the Adventurer could pass a test. Having no other choice, the Adventurer agreed to take the test, during which he met Vivita, shaman of the little fairies.
After the Adventurer passed the test, the silver haired youth showed up as promised, and introduced himself as Brandeis. Brandeis told the Adventurer that the pixies were bond by the mission concerning the Rainbow Bridge and had absolutely no chance to go to the outside world. On the other hand, the Rainbow Bridge was also the cause of his elder brother's death and his teacher's disappearance. Out of resentment, Brandeis decided to reduce the Rainbow Bridge to ruins. His determination impressed the Adventurer, and the two became allies.
After that, Brandeis revealed the next step of his plan: He was going to sneak into the Sea of Azure Clouds with an invisibility potion and blow up the magic array for repairing the Rainbow Bridge. However, an accident happened a moment later — the invisibility potion meant for Brandeis was all spilled on the Adventurer! With no time to fix the problem, the Adventurer had to blow up the magic array himself...
At the Sea of Azure Clouds, the Adventurer finished preparation and the explosion went as planned. In the permeating smoke, Brandeis appeared leading an army of little fairies, turning the situation at the sea of clouds chaotic. The pixies and little fairies were eager to fight, as the Adventurer and Hetty confronted Brandeis.
At Zanubia the high priest's order, the pixies launched their attacks at the little fairies. They were on even terms when a weird purple fog of magic suddenly took shape. The thick fog had just shrouded the whole sea of clouds when something else unexpected happened — Philly, who was fighting the little fairies, fell to the ground unconscious, and the pixies also passed out one by one in the purple fog! Seeing this, all beings present were shocked and began to panic. Zanubia suspected that Brandeis caused this. The latter argued in vain before leaving with the remaining little fairies in a hurry.
The situation had deviated from Brandeis's plan. Staring at the weird purple fog that appeared out of nowhere, Brandeis was lost in thoughts. However, that was but the tip of the conspiracy concerning pixies and the Rainbow Bridge...
To look into his brother's death, Brandeis went to Calder's former fiancée, Cecelia the "Witch of Comet" with the Adventurer, but they were baffled by Cecelia's indifference. Before they left, Cecelia gave Brandeis a crystal stone bracelet, which was left by Calder.
The Adventurer and Brandeis examined the bracelet and found a weird riddle. They went to the Time Garden according to the hint, and unexpectedly spotted Calder in the thick fog... Just when Brandeis was excited to see his brother, a mysterious power drew them into the inmost part of the garden, where they saw Brandeis's teacher, Mimir the giant of wisdom.
Mimir told the two a prophecy: "The pure dawn and star of night will find the lost treasure in the wind to restore the brilliance of the rainbow." Brandeis was the star in the prophecy, and all the happenings were related to the Rainbow Bridge. After Mimir finished, a purple fog gradually veiled the Time Garden, and Mimir fell into sleep. They now had more puzzles to solve. However, the Adventurer and Brandeis weren't aware that the tragedy was just beginning...
Brandeis and the Adventurer met Cecelia again. Seeing that they had grown closer and their teamwork improved, she was less aggressive than before. After Cecelia left, the bracelet she left let out strange light again. Following the light, the Adventurer and Brandeis unexpectedly found a string of the laurel harp. It reminded Brandeis of memories between him and his brother Calder.
According to the rest of the bracelet's riddle, the two restored the incomplete laurel harp. Brandeis played the tune in his memories, bring the two into the memories hidden in the harp. There, Brandeis saw a younger self and Calder. The words Calder said in the end untied the old knot of Brandeis's heart and addressed his attitude towards his brother. Just then, Cecelia appeared. She was actually working with Mimir in secret to lure the two to this land of memories.
Cecelia told them that both the death of Calder and the current sufferings of the pixies were caused by Goddess Freya. To stop the goddess, they must find the treasure in Mimir's prophecy. Having said this, Cecelia died because of the goddess's curse. The deaths of his brother and his teacher made Brandeis more determined to resist the goddess. The storm brought by the Rainbow Bridge was about to hit...
When searching for Brandeis, the Adventurer was attacked by the mysterious man in black and nearly killed. Brandeis arrived in time and saved him. The two realized that Goddess Freya was monitoring them, and the man in black was sent by her. The two had a talk and decided to set out in search of the treasure at once.
It seemed that the magic of stars on Brandeis somehow resonated with the treasure. After a long search, they finally found the treasure at the Blooming Land — a Ring of Falsehood with a star imprint. The two touched the ring and travelled back in time to the Mercury Palace. There, they saw the shocking truth: Calder was killed by Freya and Zanubia, and the goddess used the power of his soul to create a curse that confined the pixies. The pixies then forgot Mimir and Calder, and considered the goddess their only idol of worship. The Goddess did all of this to repair the Rainbow Bridge and return to God's Domain, where she was going to execute an even more horrible plan...
Returning from the memories in the ring, the Adventurer and Brandeis met Arcana who had been pretending to be dead. She was after the treasure. The two were no match of Arcana at her full strength. They were going to lose when Brandeis created a barrier. He entrusted the Adventurer with the Ring of Falsehood, and requested him to find the other treasure and thwart Freya's scheme. Then, Brandeis sent the Adventurer to safety while he faced Arcana alone...
2831500:
Book of Fantasy was a holy relic at Comodo, but it had been letting out an evil aura lately. The Adventurer, who was here on vacation, had to address the crisis and purify the Book of Fantasy at Aloha the village mayor's request.
Surprisingly, the Adventurer resonated with the Book of Fantasy during the purification — Dazzling light left him unconscious...
When the Adventurer woke up, he found himself in Fantasy Land, the world inside the book. Cenass the sage introduced the Adventurer to the place and arranged for him to join the Rose Drama Club's rehearsal. Through the script, the Adventurer learned about the Black Devil. It was the monster destroying the Fantasy Land, and the cause of Book of Fantasy's abnormality.
Amid the Adventurer's chat with Cenass, the town was attacked by the Black Devil. The Adventurer helped rescue the residents, but he mistook a girl with black hair and red eyes for the Black Devil in disguise. The misunderstanding was resolved, and the two fought side by side, but the girl still held a grudge, and their cooperation ended badly. After that, the Adventurer learned from Cenass that the girl was Neula, also from Comodo.
The Adventurer tried to make up with Neula, during which he came to know her better — Because of her unusual appearance, Neula was considered an "Ominous Child" by dwellers of the island, and bullied and marginalized. She resented those who treated her like a villain, and longed for acknowledgement and affection.
After much effort, the Adventurer was finally forgiven by Neula, and the two became allies. They also accidentally found the stronghold of the Black Devil, and discovered an imprisoned woman in white there. Neula recognized the woman as the crucial "Guardian" of Fantasy Land. After a bitter battle, the two defeated the devil jailor and freed the woman.
The Guardian called herself Mist, and mentioned keywords such as "witch" and "seal." The Adventurer called Cenass over for a discussion, and they finally figured out the whole picture — The cause of all trouble was a powerful evil spirit called Witch of Calamity. To break the weakening seal, she ordered her subordinates to commit crimes everywhere.
To keep the Fantasy Land peaceful, the Adventurer and his crew asked Mist for a solution, who answered that only the "girl in the prophecy" could restore the seal and stop the witch. Neula was pleased to find that she resembled the "girl in the prophecy" a lot. She then passed Mist's test and proved herself to be the savior.
Therefore, guided by Mist, the crew ventured deep into the forbidden land to take Neula to the seal. However, on their way, they were accused of being "wicked," and resisted by various creatures. Suspicious signs and Mist's increasingly bizarre attitude clouded the world-saving journey in doubts... However, Neula was already blinded by vanity. She couldn't wait to become the savior and be praised and admired by all.
Finally, the crew arrived at the seal. Neula offered her power, and Mist infused it into the seal. After a loud noise, instead of being restored, the seal broke completely, and the freed power of witch poured into Mist's body. — She was no guardian, but a clone of Witch of Calamity that had escaped the seal. The witch laughed at the deceived crew forthrightly. She called Neula her sacrifice, and wanted to devour her. The Adventurer resisted with all his might, and Cenass seized the chance to teleport the three back to the kingdom of fairy tales.
Ashamed and guilty, Neula escaped the book crying. Cenass had to lead the Fantasy Land as it faced the waking calamity. The Adventurer, on the other hand, was wondering what the relationship between the Witch of Calamity and Neula was. The answer might have its loot at Comodo...
2831501:
After the Adventurer left Comodo temporarily, he again received news about Neula: during her stay in reality, she was harassed by the Witch of Calamity again, and her soul went missing in an unknown space. With the help of the island's priest, the Adventurer entered the rift of chaos Neula was in. He travelled through various illusions, learned about Neula's miserable past, and thwarted the witch's scheme to take her away by force.
After being rescued, Neula followed the Adventurer back to Dream City. She expected to be resented and hated for releasing the witch, but instead of blaming her, residents of Dream City cared for her and forgave her. Moved by the residents' kindness, Neula decided to stop evading and remain in Dream City to fight alongside everyone else. One the other hand, Cenass shared his latest discoveries with the Adventurer: the deceased Dream Queen seemed to have left an anti-witch weapon in the Darklight Forest.
However, the Darklight Forest was then under the witch's control. The stronghold she built there stood in the way to hope. To build a powerful team, the Adventurer and Neula rallied capable people in Dream City. Despite some twists and turns, the two fulfilled their task and gradually included members such as Rona and Cliff in their solidary and fearless team. The team then headed towards the Darklight Forest.
With the assistance of the allies, the Adventurer and Neula forced through waves of enemies and advanced towards the Tree of Time deep in the forest, but a strange thick fog separated them from the rest of the team. An illusion of Dream Queen appeared under the Tree of Time and granted them the treasure chest holding the "daybreak star." However, how to defeat the witch with the "daybreak star" remained unknown.
The Adventurer and his crew had to return to Dream City with the treasure chest. As the treasure chest slowly opened, starlight flowed out, creating a curious realm in which the team members were all seeing different illusions. Neula, on the other hand, was arguing with someone and yelling in resistance... Finally, the shining daybreak star was absorbed into Neula's body, but the joy of becoming a hero wasn't found on her face. Neula said that she didn't gain any special power, and had no idea how to defeat the witch. Then, she acted out and dashed out of Dream City.
The Adventurer hurriedly followed her, eager to know what happened to Neula, but before he could get any key information, a huge noise was heard from Dream City. Some panicked residents ran to the Adventurer and Neula, and told them that the witch was attacking Dream City in order to destroy the threatening "daybreak star." On hearing this, Neula had a thorough breakdown. For some unknown purpose, she ran back to Dream City without hesitation. The Adventurer followed her closely, attempting to rescue the residents still stuck in the city.
The city, once serene and beautiful, had turned into a burning hell of death. Although the Adventurer tried hard, some allies were lost forever. Meanwhile, Cenass was also doing whatever he could to stop the witch. He was willing to sacrifice his life if that would protect the light of "daybreak star" from evil... However, something no one expected then happened — In the chaotic battle, Neula actually attacked Cenass from behind and joined the witch's side.
Laughing wildly, the Witch of Calamity flew off with Neula. Although she spared survivors of Dream City for now, the latter were more troubled now: How was the witch going to use Neula? Would the creatures in the book ever overcome the calamity? What will the Fantasy Land's future be like...
2831502:
Betrayed by Neula and losing the "daybreak star" left by the queen, the desperate residents of Dream City decided to abandon their home and leave the city to escape the witch's prosecution. Although the Adventurer was reluctant to part with everyone, he helped them pack, during which he found the discarded mystery treasure chest. The light left in the chest teleported the Adventurer into a time rift, where he again met Queen Ophelia's illusion. The queen told the Adventurer that the witch was not invincible; she had a fatal weakness. She also gave the Adventurer a hint: "The reunited friendship and trust will show the path to victory." Once he was back in reality, the Adventurer informed the residents of the news. The residents of Dream City hadn't agreed on whether to keep resisting the witch, but finally, Sage Cenass recovered in time and convinced everyone to follow the queen's prophecy and rally all possible forces to prepare for the showdown against the witch.
Since the enemies were many, the Adventurer and his crew formed an advance team to sneak into Calamity Realm — the witch's base of operation, planning to weaken the defense there first. During the exploration, the Adventurer overheard a crucial piece of intel: The witch took Neula away because she wanted to recover her own power, and she was preparing for a so-called "merging ritual." Once the ritual was complete, she would devour Neula. Of course, the Adventurer's crew wouldn't sit back and let that happen. Guided by mysterious starlight, the advance team wiped out Calamity Realm's defending forces and established teleport arrays to get reinforcements. As he ventured deeper into the witch's territory, the Adventurer once again met Neula. The Adventurer's crew tried to stop their former ally from getting to the witch, but they were too late — The witch completed the ritual regardless, and summoned Neula to her side. The Adventurer pursued her desperately, only to witness the witch devouring Neula. Aggrieved and angry, the Adventurer engaged the witch in the final battle. However, the witch was indeed overwhelming at her full strength, her charged skill knocking everyone to the floor. Just when the witch was going to kill everyone, dazzling light burst from inside her: It was the daybreak star Neula transformed into. Neula told everyone to attack the source of light, which was the witch's weak spot, as she held the witch back.
Gathering everyone's strength, the Adventurer finally managed to give the witch a critical strike, and the latter fell down, crying in pain. Meanwhile, everyone present saw Neula's memories: She didn't betray. Instead, she sacrificed herself to create a chance to defeat the witch. The memories faded away, and the crew saw a tiny pure soul at the brink of shattering. Her companions shed tears in grief, but Neula didn't seem to regret. She told them that her time at Dream City was the most enjoyable part of her life, and to protect everyone was the happiest choice she ever made. Then, she smiled brightly as she melted into dots of light. On the ground beneath her, corroded by the witch, a small bush of tiny white flowers bloomed...
2831503:
Tristan, king of Louen - Midgards Kingdom, had been missing for half a year. The vast kingdom couldn't run without a king, so its most distinct Seven Royals decided to elect a new king. Each of the seven families would nominate a candidate to participate in the election. The Adventurer was invited to this historical occasion.
However, when the Adventurer was at the palace entrance watching the Seven Royals and their retinues enter the city, he accidentally made eye contact with a royal maiden. That moment, the Adventurer had a strange vision: the palace littered with corpses, a woman kneeling on the floor crying, and blood dropping on the red carpet. It seemed to be a dream of the royal maiden, but it felt so vivid. The Adventurer found the dream unusual, and he entered the palace at once.
In the palace, members of the Seven Royals were gathering in the main hall, talking in small groups. Just one glance and the Adventurer spotted that girl alone at a corner. The girl, Agnes, was a daughter of the Reaganfelg family. She had been able to see foreseeing dreams since she was young. That was why she had come to Prontera to attend the election. On the other hand, Nihil, young master of the Heine family who secretly admired Agnes, was worried about her.
Just then, Prince Nait, son of Tristan the current king, showed up and declared firmly that he was going to succeed the throne the next day, and ordered Alice the maid to prepare the scepter, symbol of kingship. His decision was met with strong disagreement of the royal members present, but with the right to command the palace guards, Nait forced the royal members to attend his succession ceremony on the next day.
On the second day, the royal members arrived at the Room of Throne one after another. Prince Nait shook hands with all of them before he ascended the stairs leading to the throne, and accepted the bishop's blessing in front of the throne. Then, Alice came to Prince Nait, holding up a silver casket containing the scepter. The prince picked up the scepter complacently, but before he could declare his official succession, black blood dripped from the corners of his mouth, and he fell to the ground, motionless.
Everyone present was shocked. The queen immediately summoned the guards to investigate everyone present. Doctor Karl examined the prince's body and announced that he found a deadly poison in Prince Nait's palm, which would kill a person soon after contact, and the scepter was covered by the same poison. Guards found Alice the maid secretly carrying the poison on her, and since she was the last person to touch the scepter, the queen ordered the guards to take Alice to prison.
It seemed to conclude the case, but Agnes and Nihil raised some doubts. Firstly, what kind of culprit would keep such decisive evidence on them after committing the crime? Secondly, Alice was a timid girl that couldn't possibly have done this. The Adventurer, Agnes, and Nihil went to the queen together and requested permission to investigate the palace freely.
Just when the investigation of Adventurer's crew had some progress, news came that Alice's trial was scheduled for the next day. The three decided to prove Alice innocent with the evidence they found.
The trial was held as scheduled, where the three revealed the truth in front of the audience. Actually, since Alice was a coward and rumors had it that the palace was haunted, she dared not fetch the scepter from the cellar herself, and asked Guard Captain Martin to get it for her in the dead of night and put it in the bishop's silver casket. Alice didn't touch the scepter during the whole process, so she didn't have the chance to apply the poison.
Although Alice was proved innocent during the trial, there were still many doubts. Since the poison was found on Alice, Nihil asked her whether anyone approached her on the day of the murder. Alice recalled that she was knocked to the ground by Paulos Richard, which provided a new target for investigation. After thorough research of Paulos, The Adventurer's crew confirmed that he was the real culprit.
Nihil reported the truth to the queen, and summoned everyone to the Room of Throne for another trial. The Adventurer identified Paulos as the real murderer of the prince, and used evidence to recreate the process. Actually, Paulos applied the poison not to the scepter, but to his own glove. When the prince arrived and shook hand with him, he touched the poison and died. When everyone's attention was drawn to the prince, Paulos put the poisoned glove on a statue's hand, so that the guards wouldn't find it on him.
Now that the case had been solved, the queen ordered the guards to take Paulos into custody. Just then, Agnes fainted all of a sudden, shocking everyone again. On the other hand, the Adventurer saw another of Agnes's foreseeing dreams, different from the last one. The palace was going to see more trouble...
2831505:
Queen Catharine called an urgent meeting and announced that the election would be held on the next day. This abrupt decision worried the nobles. Agnes also saw signs of disasters in her foreseeing dream. To prevent any accident, the Adventurer's crew tried to talk the queen into delaying the election.
However, Queen Catharine was quite stubborn. She refused to change her plan even after the Adventurer presented the threatening letter Arish Narius received and explained that some dangerous force was trying to disrupt the election. Having no better choice, the Adventurer had to accept her arrangement. When heading to the guest house, the Adventurer saw two knights carrying a storage box out of the Eternal Palace.
At midnight, a tragedy happened as expected: Prince Ernst was burned to death in his room, his charred body a painful sight. The Adventurer's crew started their investigation at once. However, it seemed that the culprit was identified even before they could sort through the evidence found at the site — Helmut claimed to have seen Peter starting the fire, and since Peter's defense was unconvincing, he was imprisoned as the suspect.
Based on what he knew about Peter, Nihil believed that he didn't kill Ernst, but to prove it, the Adventurer's crew needed more evidence. Agnes took out a bronze key with a mark of the banquet hall, and suggested that they further investigate the bistro and the kitchen. The three made an arrangement to meet on the next morning.
However, when the Adventurer went to the banquet hall to investigate, Fernando the palace manager refused to cooperate. The Adventurer had to search somewhere else first. The Adventurer's crew then found many combustible items in the prince's room that should be in the kitchen. The Adventurer pressed Fernando again, and was told that there was a theft at the kitchen the day before Ernst's death.
The Adventurer reexamined the evidence he had and found out how the culprit started the fire, proving that Ernst wasn't killed by Peter's fire magic. However, it wasn't enough to prove Peter's innocence — Peter could sense flames and should have been able to prevent the prince's death. To bring to light whether Peter murdered the prince remotely, the Adventurer started to investigate Peter.
In the room Peter was staying, the Adventurer found a book affected by a spell, in which there was a mysterious letter: It turned out that on the night of the murder, Peter was not in the room, but somewhere far from the fire site, meeting a mystery person secretly. Nihil wanted to identify the letter's sender. It was the only way to prove Peter's innocence.
To do so, the Adventurer followed the clue on the envelop and went to question Ipa the royal knight. However, Ipa felt guilty and ran off on seeing the Adventurer. When pursuing Ipa, the Adventurer was stopped by the queen's guard captain. Although the Adventurer managed to defeat him, he also lost Ipa.
Fortunately, there was another clue: the scent left on the letter. The Adventurer followed Agnes's advice and went to Rose Theater to ask the noble ladies, who were familiar with perfumes, for clues. After the investigation, the Adventurer's crew concluded that the mysterious sender was actually Queen Catharine.
Catharine was Ernst's mother, so she wouldn't harm him. Therefore, Nihil thought that they've got all the necessary evidence, and decided with the Adventurer and Agnes to hold another trial on the second day to exonerate Peter.
The Adventurer had a debate with Helmut during the trial and, by reproducing the process of the fire, proved that Peter didn't burn the prince to death. The Adventurer also presented the letter in the book, and explained why Peter failed to save the prince. The audience were gossiping about Peter and Catharine's secret meeting when Catharine stopped the commotion and asked Peter to describe what really happened that night.
After hearing Peter's description, the crowd agreed that he was innocent, but the trial hadn't ended. Nihil suspected that the prince had already fainted or died before the fire, and requested a further autopsy to find clues to the true culprit, but Catharine didn't want any more destruction to her son's body. After an argument, she ordered the trial to end, and took the prince's body, planning to have it buried five days later.
The Adventurer and the rest could only seek clues via other means. Just then, Walter sent a subordinate to meet the Adventurer in secret. He claimed that Queen Catharine was the prince's murderer, and provided evidence. In return, Walter asked the Adventurer to help him find the real murderer of Isenhardt while investigating the queen. To reveal the truth, the Adventurer agreed to work with Walter for now.
The Adventurer went to feel Queen Catharine out, but she was away from the palace transporting the prince's body to the church. The queen also ordered the royal guards to stop the Adventurer from entering Eternal Palace. Nihil suggested that they ask the servants for intel first.
Servant Averell told the Adventurer something curious — Ernst had a quarrel with Catharine the night before his death, and there seemed to be a third person in the room. To find out the truth, the Adventurer's crew knocked the royal guards out and burst into the queen's bedroom.
Traces in the bedroom did show that there was a verbal, or even physical fight. More surprisingly, there was a secret cellar in the queen's bedroom, where an unknown man seemed to have been living. The Adventurer's crew were about to have a discussion, when Queen Catharine came back from the church. Furious, she summoned her guards, trying to drive the invaders out of the palace.
The Adventurer defeated Catharine's guards, and forced her to sit down and talk. After an inquiry, Catharine admitted that she was hiding a lover in her bedroom. Ernst discovered this, and had a conflict with her. However, she denied having killed Ernst for it.
Catharine's confession sounded logical, but there were still some doubts. The Adventurer questioned Catharine further with the evidence at hand. When he presented a pile of blank letters, a heart lock appeared on Catharine as expected, but she dodged the question with smart lies. To reveal what Catharine was hiding, the Adventurer decided to visit Walter again for help.
The Adventurer shared with Walter what he discovered at Eternal Palace. On seeing the blank letters, Walter became pale. He asked the Adventurer to splash water on the letters, revealing words: a series of schemes targeting candidates to the throne. Even Martin the guard captain was involved. He bribed Andrew into assassinating Isenhardt.
Anguished, Walter worked with the Adventurer to lure Martin into an underground prison for an inquiry. Martin failed to handle the pressure and a heart lock was revealed. It turned out that the lover the queen mentioned was the king himself. The king wasn't missing. He went into hiding to wipe out other candidates from behind the scenes.
Meanwhile, Martin also disclosed a more bizarre fact: the king, who should have been pulling strings in the cellar at Eternal Palace, had gone missing, and the queen was concealing this fact on purpose.
It seemed that Queen Catharine was at the core of all the cases after all, but the queen firmly refused to be investigated, and the Adventurer could do nothing about it. However, Walter said with confidence that he could solve the problem with informers in the palace. So, the Adventurer's crew went back to the guesthouse to rest, planning to continue the investigation on the second day.
Walter found Frank the reporter, and the latter said that he once heard a loud noise in the Dawn Garden at midnight. The Adventurer went to the garden. After searching and deducting, the crew arrived at a horrible conclusion: the king had probably been pushed off Eternal Palace's balcony and died from the injury.
However, the king's body was nowhere to be found. Just when the crowd were scratching their heads, the Adventurer recalled something — Before the arson, the queen had a large storage box sent into the prince's guest room. That night, there was a big fire at the room, leaving only a charred body.
Was the king's body in the box? Was the victim really Prince Ernst? These questions lingered in everyone's mind. They needed evidence to solve them. Therefore, the Adventurer's crew forced through the queen's cordon, defeated the resisting royal captain and arrived at the coffin of the "prince." The forensic pathologist did another autopsy and found that it was not Ernst, but King Tristan George.
Hearing that the king was dead, Walter let out lunatic laughter. He seemed to be satisfied, and was going to leave Prontera. However, the Adventurer still shouldered the duties of a royal detective: He must identify the victim and make the murderer receive due punishment.
With complex feelings, the Adventurer's crew left the cemetery. Behind them, the defeated royal captain was back. The reason he was protecting the queen seemed to be more than loyalty...
The Adventurer's crew entered the Room of Throne and interrupted the memorial service Queen Catharine was holding. Nihil revealed that the victim was the king. The queen kept denying and making excuses, but faced with solid evidence, she finally went speechless and the secrets in her heart were exposed.
The Adventurer entered Catharine's World of Heart to seek her true reason for killing King Tristan. There, the Adventurer saw the queen's miserable past: She and the king's marriage was sheerly of convenience. The king never showed her any love or respect. The gloomy life was driving her to a breakdown, and Ernst was her only support. The queen's only wish was to be with her son, even if Ernst was made a minstrel and couldn't call her mother. However, Isenhardt's death estranged the prince from the king. During their fight, the prince pushed the king off the balcony by accident. To exempt her son from the death penalty, Catharine made up the arson.
Knowing that she no longer stood a chance, Queen Catharine decided to sacrifice herself. She begged the Adventurer to keep part of the truth a secret, and try her as the king's murderer, so that Ernst, who had escaped, wouldn't be pursued. However, not even such a humble wish was granted — Walter suddenly showed up with a large crowd of royal members. They were actually eavesdropping throughout this special "trial."
Regardless of the reasons behind the case, the cruel and inflexible royal members wanted to kill Ernst and Catharine to uphold the royal family's authority and dignity. The queen cried in despair, but was saved by the royal captain, who appeared from nowhere. He was no one other than Ernst. Worried about his mother, he never escaped Louen as planned, and had been waiting in the church. On the other hand, Walter revealed his fangs — he sent all his private forces at the queen and the prince, planning to kill them on the spot to honor his beloved son Isenhardt.
To uphold justice, and out of sympathy for the queen and the prince, the Adventurer volunteered to stop Walter and his subordinates. Ernst also fought with all his might, as he escorted Catharine towards the palace gate. Suddenly, an unexpected arrow came flying at Ernst's back. Without much thought, Catharine opened her arms to cover her son, and the arrow penetrated her chest.
The mother, trapped in the palace for her entire life, failed to escape it after all. The son, left alone in the mortal world, had lost his purpose of living. The desperate Ernst picked up Catharine's body and moved towards the palace gate in the rain of arrows, but in the end, neither of them managed to reach the freedom one step away...
2831506:
The Book of Yimir, the holy work full of hero's power disappeared from the Unlimited Library. Meanwhile, the spirit in the sealed magic sword also escaped the Tower of Thanatos and went missing. Rathgricy the Valkyrie sensed the remaining traces of the magic sword in the Unlimited Library, and realized that the magic sword had stollen the Book of Yimir. Rathgricy requested the Adventurer to protect a gemstone that should have been inlaid in the title page of Book of Yimir. It was the only item that could enable and use the hero's power in the book. To use the Book of Yimir's power, the magic sword must get the Fate Gem, but the gem had always been kept by the girl sleeping in the spring at the roots of Yggdrasil. During the crisis, the Adventurer was tasked with seeking the gem and the Book of Yimir.
In search of the Fate Gem, the Adventurer went to Hvergelmir. Nidhogg didn't trust this unexpected visitor. Thanatos showed up at their encounter and prevented a conflict.
