Strangely, Nidhogg referred to Thanatos as her younger sister. Nidhogg told the Adventurer that a short while ago, Thanatos's spirit appeared in her dream. Nidhogg sensed the power of her younger sister Vedrfolnir in Thanatos. She was sure that Thanatos was the reincarnation of Vedrfolnir. Although Nidhogg had no idea why Thanatos's spirit would appear in her dream, she missed her sister so much, that she didn't hesitate to use her power to take Thanatos out of the dream. However, as a spirit, Thanatos didn't have his previous power or memories, and was even a bit confused. He had to rely on Nidhogg's power to survive. After Nidhogg found out what the Adventurer was here for, she offered to give him the gem. But she hoped that the Adventurer could escort Thanatos's spirit to Niflheim with her, because only Hela the Goddess of Death knew how to save spirits stuck between life and death. As she had just woken up and had used up much power, she needed the Adventurer's company to go to the land of the death.
2831507:
But Nidhogg was totally unaware of this. She suggested that they use the Fate Gem as a bait to lure the book thief into a trap and capture them after they entered the Dragon Species' Secret Realm. Her plan attracted a mysterious shadow that wanted to rob the Fate Gem. Defeated by the Adventurer and Thanatos, the shadow revealed their real look — a girl that looked exactly like Nidhogg! Only then did Nidhogg realize that Thanatos was really not her younger sister. The girl in front of them was the true Vedrfolnir. Ved begged her sister to forgive and save her, but Thanatos discovered that Vedrfolnir was lying. However, although Nidhogg was shocked to see her sister alive, she chose to help her. Despite the Adventurer and Thanatos's objection, Nidhogg used the Fate Gem to activate the Book of Yimir and restore Vedrfolnir's power.
Nidhogg poured all her power into maintaining the Fate Gem, and shut down all her senses, while Vedrfolnir stopped the Adventurer and Thanatos from approaching Nidhogg. As she regained her power, Vedrfolnir revealed her true purpose. Everything since Thanatos's soul entered Nidhogg's dream was part of her scheme to take advantage of her sister's care and seize the power of Yimir's heart. However, just when she was going to slay the two triumphantly, Nidhogg opened her eyes and closed the Book of Yimir, causing its light to fade away. Vedrfolnir turned around and stared at her elder sister in confusion. Nidhogg stretched out one hand and spotlighted Thanatos with a golden beam, Thanatos burst out of the light and charged at Vedrfolnir, weapon in hand. Vedrfolnir threatened Thanatos, telling him that he would die if he killed her, since his spirit relied on the magic sword to stay alive. Nevertheless, Thanatos's sword penetrated Vedrfolnir without hesitation. Vedrfolnir screamed in pain as she questioned her elder sister why she did this, to which Nidhogg replied that, although she valued Vedrfolnir's life as much as her own life, she valued every life in the world equally. Vedrfolnir was killed, and the hero's power she had absorbed returned to pages, which fluttered in the air and were scattered across the world by the impact. Everything was back to tranquility. Nidhogg fell to the ground. Thanatos, who had almost disappeared, lent her a hand to pull her back to her feet. To her surprise, he turned into a page of the Book of Yimir in her hand.
Nidhogg burst into tears. She saw Thanatos's memories in the Book of Yimir. It turned out that Vedrfolnir joined Morroc in betraying Nidhogg, but was discovered and defeated by Nidhogg. Deprived of a vessel for spirit, she went to the Abyssal Lake and possessed Hogne the magic sword. After that, instead of falling asleep as she herself claimed, Vedrfolnir eroded Thanatos as the magic sword. Therefore, she closed the Book of Yimir and transferred the memories to Thanatos, but after regaining his memories, Thanatos again chose to save the world with his own life. Nidhogg thought that since her selfish decision nearly caused a disaster, she was a disqualified guardian of the Fate Gem. She gave the Fate Gem to the Adventurer, and tasked him with the hard mission of retrieving all the pages. After that, Nidhogg fell into sleep again. Maybe she could reunite with Thanatos in her dreams.
2831508:
After the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn boarded the fleet of the Walters, they were hit by something unknown at sea. There was a deafening noise, and everyone on board fainted.
When they woke up, the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn found themselves in a mysterious scorching place. Guided by a turtle, they found the injured sailors and treated them. In this place, Hollgrehenn's prayers always worked, leading him into believing that it was his place of luck.
The crew followed the turtle further and found Ian Walter, but behind him stood the mysterious girl Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer saw on the Turtle Island. She seemed to have drifted to this place with Walter's fleet in search of something.
After an investigation, the Adventurer found that there used to be a human's village here, inhabited by Old Ryos, but they were swallowed by some huge monster, and were still in its stomach! No wonder that the sailors couldn't locate the Turtle Island. The island was actually alive and swimming around.
Just then, Hollgrehenn found a giant furnace with magical powers. Overjoyed, he was going to forge Phantom Equipment with it, when the mysterious girl suddenly started to attack the furnace. Hollgrehenn pushed her to the ground, causing her veil to drop. She was actually Sara Alin — Freya's saint.
Sara Alin claimed that the furnace was the monster's heart. To kill the monster and protect the continent from worse disasters, she must destroy the heart. Ian followed her, claiming that he had to destroy the furnace and protect Alberta.
Hollgrehenn, on the other hand, thought that the furnace could heal everyone's wounds, and wasn't as evil as they imagined. Just when they were quarreling, a general-like turtle appeared to expel them all. The crew defeated the turtle general, but before they could land the final blow, rocks began to fall. An earthquake hit the Old Ryo Palace, and everyone fainted again.
They woke up to find themselves back at the port of Alberta. Some members, such as Ian, were seriously injured and brought back by Isenhour for rehabilitation. The crew's description reminded Isenhour of something relevant. He asked the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn to see him at his house the next day.
2831509:
The cold snap at Alberta was getting worse. The Adventurer and Hollgrehenn went to the Walter Residence. Isenhour showed them to the family library, where he had found some clues concerning the Turtle Island.
According to him, the Turtle Island's appearance was related to a previous cold snap, which was caused by the Frost Staff — an artifact of jötunn. To seek help, Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer went to the Moon Lake to find jötunn's children, Fenrir and Jörmungandr.
Fenrir agreed to help, and took the two to where the Frost Staff fell with a portal of space. On the way, they met many ice monsters, which were all materialized by the Frost Staff's conscious. It seemed to be protecting something desperately.
Fenrir and Jörmungandr used the Force of Blood Vessel to lift the Frost Staff's seal and resonate with it. They found that the Frost Staff was dropped by Angrboda the jötunn when he was fighting the gods in order to bring the three siblings back. It then brought humanity a horrible disaster. Curiously enough, the cold snap didn't spread, and the Midgards continent was unharmed. It might have something to do with the Old Ryos.
To find the truth, Fenrir gave the Soulforge Stone to Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer for them to use at the Old Ryo ruins. Maybe it could summon the spirit of an Old Ryo member, who could tell them what actually happened.
When they got back to Alberta, the worried Isenhour was already waiting for them in front of Hollgrehenn's smithy. He had decided to escort Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer to the Turtle Island with his subordinates to reveal the truth and protect Alberta!
2831510:
Alberta was hit by a cold snap, causing huge damage to its fishery and shipping industry. As the lords of Alberta, the Walters suffered a large decrease in tax revenue. In addition, some Alberta residents went missing, bringing uneasiness to everyone.
Ian Walter the patriarch remembered the Adventurer, who solved the case of the Seven Royals. Although they were enemies, faced with a crisis, Ian decided to put the old grudge on the back burner and send for the Adventurer.
The Adventurer agreed to come. On the way, he met Hollgrehenn on the ship, who was also heading for Alberta. After arriving at the port, Hollgrehenn parted ways with the Adventurer excitedly and went away quickly.
After the Adventurer got to the Walter Residence, Ian Walter explained the details of the request to him, requesting him to investigate the case thoroughly and find the missing citizens, promising to pay him well. Just when the Adventurer was about to leave, he saw Hollgrehenn being stopped by the guards at the gate of the mansion.
It turned out that Hollgrehenn was planning to open a smithy of his own in Alberta, but the location he preferred was owned by the Walters, so he had come for a cheeky negotiation. Persuaded by the Adventurer, the butler agreed to sell the shop front to Hollgrehenn. To thank the Adventurer, Hollgrehenn volunteered to help with his investigation.
The two went to the Ocean Inn, a place most frequented by local sailors, for clues. After an investigation, they found that the missing residents were probably drugged and took to a horrible island called the Turtle Island.
They reported back to Ian, who asked them to go to the Turtle Island for more clues, and light the lighthouse on the island to assist the landing of the Walters' fleet. To complete Ian Walter's quest, the two must find a way to get to the Turtle Island.
They went to Web, a scholar who specialized in studying the Turtle Island, but the stuffy scholar mistook them for gold diggers and challenged them to a series of tests, because he would only provide intel to true adventurers.
The two had to go to the port for another investigation. There, they finally had a general idea about the Turtle Island, and learned that to get onto the island, they needed a relic called the Flame Compass. They reported back to Web, but just when Web was going to acknowledge them, the little turtle he kept ran away. After the Adventurer retrieved it, it still sought more adventure, so Web had to entrust the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn with it. He also gave them the Flame Compass.
Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer finally could head to the Turtle Island. However, as it was already too late for a voyage, the two decided to have a rest and set off once the weather turned sunny.
2831511:
After resting, Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer got onto the Turtle Island with the help of the little turtle. It was incredibly hot on the island, and the Adventurer had a heatstroke and collapsed. Luckily, he was saved by the chilly elixir Hollgrehenn made. Just when the two were refreshed and going to explore the island, a mysterious veiled woman appeared. Hollgrehenn fell in love on seeing this tall and elegant woman, but before he could hit on her, the veiled woman spotted them and left.
Disappointed, Hollgrehenn resumed the island exploration with the Adventurer, and found that the missing people were not devoured by a turtle as rumors said, but abducted by the Arunafeltz States' radical followers of Goddess Freya and turned into miners, maybe because of the island's precious Frost Fire Crystal deposit.
Frost Fire Crystals could be forged into Phantom Equipment, which interested Hollgrehenn, but their top priority was to save the missing residents of Alberta.
During the search, the two were discovered by a lookout of the radicals. After a good fight, the two finally sneaked into a hidden cave on the Turtle Island, and found the missing residents. However, they were hypnotized by the radicals, and some were put in iron cages. To save them, the two must disable the device and forge an omni key.
Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer managed to save the residents, but they also alerted the subordinates of the radicals. They covered the residents while fighting the enemies, and finally reached the port and lighted the Walters' lighthouse.
Guided by the little turtle, the crew returned to Alberta. Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer went to the Walter Residence and reported back to Ian Walter.
Ian was mad at the fact that the culprits were the Arunafeltz States' radicals. He would not allow such threats near his territory, so he decided to set out with the Walter fleet and following the light from the lighthouse to get onto the Turtle Island and eliminate the enemies.
Having learned about Hollgrehenn's personality, Ian Walter awarded him the title of royal blacksmith and new attires. Overjoyed, Hollgrehenn agreed to go to the Turtle Island with them to repay Lord Walter. Requested by Hollgrehenn, who promised to forge equipment for him, the Adventurer had to set out with Sun Chaser, the Walters' ship. Ian Walter dispatched his fleet contentedly, and Hollgrehenn was overwhelmed by excitement, not knowing that the voyage would reveal a bigger secret about the Turtle Island and plunge everyone into a graver crisis.
2831512:
Isenhour led the sailors, the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn to the island again. Guided by Turdy, the crew arrived at the entrance of the Old Ryo Palace. When they finally forced through the vines blocking the entrance, they were greeted by countless guards.
The inside of the Old Ryo Palace was overrun by monster that wanted to obstruct them, but the crew combined their power and approached the furnace step by step. When they finally reached the destination, Hollgrehenn reminded the Adventurer to use the Soulforge Stone. The secret of the Old Ryos was about to be revealed.
In the vision, some pious figures were kowtowing. Were they praying, mourning, or performing some sort of ritual? Holy particles gathered towards the furnace. After a flash of white light, Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer found themselves in a weird place.
There, they saw Quiller's memories. It turned out that the Old Ryos were descendants of Heimdallr the guardian, and were born with the power to grant wishes. However, there was no free lunch in the world. The Old Ryos would transform into turtles once the wishes were granted.
After the Frost Staff fell into the sea, Norn told the Old Ryos that "The power of frost would bring winter to the land. A thousand years later, the Wind of Fate will come with the seed of spring." However, human beings were dying. How could they live to see that day?
Chief of the Old Ryos thus made a difficult decision. He combined the power of all Old Ryos to turn himself into a giant turtle with a burning furnace for heart. He would then circulate the Frost Staff swimming to melt the ice and protect the continent.
The chief thought the decision sinful, but it was a responsibility the Old Ryos must shoulder. For him, immortality was the most dreadful penalty, but his people accepted their fate easily, and apologized to the chief, who was going to suffer in place of them.
After grasping the whole picture, Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer left the Old Ryo chief's space of memories, and the chief emerged due to the Soulforge Stone's effect. He introduced himself as Quiller, chief and wrongdoer of the Old Ryo.
Quiller said that he had been waiting for the seed in the oracle. The Turtle Island was created to protect humans, but it could no longer do so, because the wish power of the Old Ryo was fading and his soul was weakening. That had led to the cold snap in Alberta, for which he was very sorry.
Hollgrehenn was impressed by the selflessness of Quiller and the Old Ryos. Just then, Sara Alin appeared and attempted to destroy the furnace despite the others' objection.
It was actually a scheme of the Arunafeltz States. Sara Alin was here to destroy the furnace and get its core. That the Adventurer's crew summoned Quiller's spirit was a perfect chance for her.
However, Quiller said something astonishing: He referred to Sara Alin as "child of my old friend" and declared that he would restore Sara Alin's memories for her, because her current memories were shrouded by falsehood.
After a flash of white light, Sara Alin fell to the ground shouting, "Why did you deceive me?" Soothed by the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn, Sara Alin calmed down a bit. She looked at Quiller and asked him whether she should follow the path in her heart.
Quiller told Sara Alin to accept her fate. Just then, something unexpected happened. Sara Alin attacked the crew, and seized an opening to pierce Quiller's spirit with her sword. Quiller's spirit shattered, and the furnace broke into pieces following the noise.
Hollgrehenn threw himself on Sara Alin, risking his life to stop her, but she knocked him away with a palm strike. The woman glanced down at Hollgrehenn, then left with the furnace's core.
Without the furnace, the Old Ryo Palace was soon frozen. Isenhour and the sailors wanted to take Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer out of the place, but the roads were all blocked by ice and monsters.
Fortunately, Fenrir descended from the sky and protected the crew with a barrier made of divine power, and took them back to Alberta. However, although he could save the Adventurer's crew, he couldn't stop the cold snap from spreading.
Nevertheless, Fenrir left his token to the Adventurer. He seemed to believe that the "Wind of Fate" could change fate, and told the Adventurer to call him when he needed help.
The usually cheerful Hollgrehenn was abnormally silent. He told the Adventurer to leave him alone, during which he would go to Walter's library. Maybe he could find something useful.
An endless winter had come, a knell tolling for humanity. However, would there be a second Old Ryo in the world?
2831513:
The cold snap almost stuck everyone. Hollgrehenn waited for the Adventurer in front of the Walter Residence with Isenhour as promised. While others shivered, Hollgrehenn was covered with sweat, claiming that he had found a way to save the continent from a song in myths. 
        The Adventurer and their crew summoned Fenrir and Jörmungandr with a token. Hollgrehenn sang the song, and the two gods told the Adventurer that the materials mentioned in the song were the Genesis Metal cast from Oridecon, the Everwood, which will never burn out, the unfreezing water of Moon Lake, and the Live Coal that can repel frost.
        Hollgrehenn said that he could find the Live Coal, Fenrir promised to fetch water from the Moon Lake, and Ian will lead the Walter family and the reinforcing royal knights to find Everwood, but the art of casting Genesis Metal, the most precious material, had been lost. Only the three dwarf brothers from the Prison were capable of it.
        However, the swarf brothers were cunning and treacherous, and the Prison was a dangerous place. Although Jörmungandr could take the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn there, he didn't believe they could survive it.
        Hollgrehenn, though, swore to come back with the Genesis Metal to forge the furnace and save the continent. Moved by Hollgrehenn's determination, Jörmungandr agreed to help him, and told the two that he would rip the Prison open at the right time for them to escape.
        As soon as the Adventurer and Hollgrehenn arrived at the Prison, the majestical warden sent jailers to drive them out, saying that they would pay a high price if they stayed. Nevertheless, Hollgrehenn refused to back down. The two went through a lot before they finally found the three dwarf brothers: Nelnis, Mildam, and Dain I.
        However, the three dwarves were as cunning as Jörmungandr and Fenrir said, and taunted Hollgrehenn heartlessly. Although they taught him how to cast Genesis Metal, it felt like just a step of a conspiracy.
        Hollgrehenn endured the taunting and, finally blessed by the Holy Light, he managed to craft the Genesis Metal with the power of light and hope, but was only greeted by the eldest dwarf's laughter, who said that Hollgrehenn could never leave the place.
        Just then, the mysterious warden appeared. Now that Hollgrehenn and the Adventurer had found out too much about dwarf arts, he wouldn't let them leave the Prison. Even though Hollgrehenn explained that he was only trying to save the continent and everyone, the warden refused to let them go.
        The Adventurer and Hollgrehenn struggled to defeat the warden, and left the Prison with Jörmungandr's help, the dwarf brothers laughing and cursing at their backs.
        A severely injured Ian and the knights brought the Everwood. Fenrir, who got frostbite, brought Moon Lake water. Looking at the Genesis Metal in his hands, Hollgrehenn announced that they had got all the materials, and he would get Live Coal, the last one.
        Hollgrehenn, the Adventurer and Isenhour revisited the Old Ryo Palace. The alter where Quiller's heart had been kept laid in ruins. Hollgrehenn looked around and started forging the furnace.
        The precious Genesis Metal lured countless monsters over. The Adventurer and Isenhour struggled to keep them at bay, but the monsters were gaining power. Just as they were about to lose, a curious power emerged from Hollgrehenn and repelled the monsters for the Adventurer and Isenhour, just like the amazing furnace.
        However, flames rose around Hollgrehenn too, threatening to engulf him.
        Isenhour and the Adventurer urged Hollgrehenn to stop, but the latter was absorbed in forging and oblivious of the flames. The Adventurer threw themselves at Hollgrehenn, trying to put out the fire, only to find themselves seeing Hollgrehenn's memories.
        The Adventurer saw that: Hollgrehenn, despite being rejected by the old blacksmith of the village due to lack of talents, refused to give up; he learned superb techniques from Hayward, but couldn't make out the thing that his master said was more important to a blacksmith than skills; Hayward handed the key to the smithy to Hollgrehenn and followed his destiny resolutely; Hollgrehenn finally learned the meaning of protecting. 
        The Adventurer discovered Hollgrehenn's secret at last, which was also the reason of his recent abnormality.
        It turned out that Sara Alin's conducts were acquiesced to by Quiller. She needed to leave with the furnace core, while Quiller had too old a soul to carry out his mission. They both chose Hollgrehenn as the seed of destiny in the prophesy. During the fight earlier, Sara Alin implanted the Live Coal of the Old Ryo clan into Hollgrehenn's body.
        That was the last material and the most important step of furnace forging.
        However, just like the Old Ryo clan paying their price, Hollgrehenn also needed to burn his own life to light a bright fire in the furnace.
        The Adventurer, who had understood everything including Hollgrehenn's fate, left Hollgrehenn's space of memories and tried to stop Hollgrehenn, but Hollgrehenn hammered the furnace for the last three times determinedly, offering his own life as its sacrifice.
        Hollgrehenn stopped breathing, and was unresponsive to the Adventurer and Isenhour's calls. When Fenrir and Jörmungandr arrived, Hollgrehenn was already gone. The grieved crowd held a hero's funeral for Hollgrehenn.
        Just then, bits and pieces of Wish Power filled the Old Ryo Palace, and an old song and call could be heard from afar, "The seed that protects humans shouldn't be left asleep in the ground. Remaining Wish Power, heed my last wish.”
        Fenrir was confused. He sensed life returning to Hollgrehenn's body.
        It turned out that the Old Ryo clan used dormant Wish Power to save Hollgrehenn. The bloodline of a deity's descendent offered blessings buried in winter to the seeds of spring.
        The furnace stopped the cold snap, the agreeable climate was restored at Alberta, making it the paradise at sea again. Perhaps, just as Quiller once said, humans, so fragile compared to giants and gods, and not even as strong as monsters, only managed to survive until the day because heroes emerged from them in troubled times.
        Live Coal goes on in everyone's heart and lights up the path for humans.

2832619:
1. After the GvG ends, a 10-min [City Settlement] period starts. When the current GvG match ends, leaders of guilds that have temporarily captured the cities must pick 1 city within the given time as the city they will finally capture. 
2. In the current GvG match, if a guild has once captured a city that was an [empty city] at the start of the battle, the city becomes the guild's [potential city]. When the city is abandoned by its final capturer, it's added to the [selectable cities] of its last capturer guild. The same process is repeated until one guild captures it. If there's no more former capturer and no guild chooses to capture the city, the city becomes an empty city again. 
3.When the current GvG match ends, if a guild has temporarily captured a city that [wasn't an empty city] at the start of the battle and abandons it, the city will be added to the [selectable cities] of its owner guild before the battle. 
4. When a guild captures multiple cities temporarily, its leader can choose one of the [selectable cities] to [directly capture]. 
5. If a guild chooses to [directly capture] a city other than its original city, its original city will be added as a [potential city] to the [selectable cities] of other guilds that have temporarily captured the city once during the current GvG match, and offered to its former capturers in reverse chronological order until there's no more capturer and no guild chooses to capture it. Then it will become an empty city again. 
6. When this GvG match ends, if a guild fails to capture its original city, the guild leader can choose to [capture the first-choice city] and then [choose 1 alternative] city temporarily captured by them. If the original city is abandoned by its temporary capturer, the guild can capture it, otherwise the guild will capture the alternative city. 
7. Cities not [directly captured] or [listed as alternative] will be abandoned, and added automatically to the [selectable cities] of its capturer guild before this GvG match. 
8. You cannot change your mind once you've selected a city. Leaders, please select prudently.
9. If you don't choose in time, the system will choose for you, prioritizing the [original city] over the [largest city]. It picks the [largest city] from among the temporarily captured cities and the available potential cities. 
10. After this GvG match ends, the following don't need to choose: guilds that owned no city last week and only one city this week, guilds that only own their original cities, and guilds that have captured no city and own no potential city.

[c][3333cc]Game rules[-][/c]
1. Rewards of the spinner [c][ff9900]cannot be obtained repeatedly[-][/c]. When you draw a duplicate reward, the round ends, and the spinner auto-resets for free.
2. During the event, Big Cat Man will offer the Adventurers free spinner attempts. Try your luck now!

[c][3333cc]Lucky Spin[-][/c]
1. Adventurers can get their preferred jackpot with one pull if they are lucky, or claim all rewards in one go with the "Lucky Spin"!
2. If you hit the same grid more than once with "Lucky Spin," the spinner [c][ff9900]won't reset[-][/c], and you are [c][ff9900]guaranteed[-][/c] a new reward every [c][ff9900]3 draws[-][/c].
3. Reminder: The fewer rewards on the spinner, the more likely you will get the jackpot, and the more "Lucky Spins" consumed.
4. Adventurers who want to get all the rewards fast are recommended to use the "Lucky Spin."

[c][3333cc]About the pool[-][/c]
1. Tap a spinner grid to check its content.
2. When you hit the same grid the second time in a round, or you have obtained all rewards of one certain grid, you get one "reserve reward."

[c][3333cc]Lucky Poring Coin[-][/c]
1. Lucky Poring Coins obtained from the spinner can be exchanged for a hidden jackpot!
2. Both types of Poring Coins are stored in the Coin Pouch and can be used anytime.
3. Poring Coins never expire, but the rewards they can be exchanged for differ by event.

[c][3333cc]About resetting[-][/c]
1. When you draw a duplicate reward or have drawn all the spinner rewards of this round, the round ends, and the spinner auto-resets for free.
2. Adventurers can reset manually, but please note that it costs 6 Big Cat Coins~

The adventurer returned to the divine tree and found that it had indeed grown a bit. The adventurer visited Maple again, and Maple said that his vision had improved somewhat; at the same time, after seeing the evil spirit, he remembered something. Maple asked the adventurer to find a mysterious place, and after some investigation, the adventurer learned that the place Maple wanted to find was Moonlight Grotto.

The adventurer entered Moonlight Grotto and began the investigation, eventually discovering the Memory Box in a crystal tree. After opening the Memory Box, the adventurer obtained a scroll and a knowing bird. The knowing bird told the adventurer that the scroll belonged to Gunn and described past events.

Just then, a flame emerged from the cave - the evil spirit suddenly appeared and tried to launch a surprise attack on the adventurer. In the critical moment, the scroll emitted a burst of power, protecting the adventurer and dispelling the evil spirit's disguise. The adventurer was surprised to find that the true identity of this evil spirit was identical to Maple!

The exposed evil spirit left in anger and frustration. The adventurer escaped from the sea of fire unscathed, with countless questions in his heart, looking for someone to answer them.
2844263:
Elly unlocked the seal of the cave, and the adventurers entered to find that the evil spirits had set up a formation to distort the Memory Box and draw evil power from it.
After the adventurers destroyed the formation, the evil spirit awoke in anger, scolding Gunn for his betrayal and vowing to destroy Luoyang. Bijou also sent her puppets to interfere with the adventurers, instructing the evil spirit to take the Memory Box and destroy the divine tree at all costs.
After defeating Bijou's Puppet, the adventurers chased the evil spirit and finally defeated it in front of the divine tree, but the evil spirit refused to vanish. At this moment, Maple - or Ulo reappeared, purifying the resentment of the evil spirit and absorbing its lost half body.
The crisis in Wasteland was resolved, but the adventurers had to bid farewell to Ulo: due to the use of the power of the divine tree, Ulo would merge with it and fall into a deep sleep. Ulo comforted the lost adventurers and asked his new friend to continue admiring the red maple of Wasteland on his behalf...
2844264:
After Ulo's soul fell asleep, the Wasteland patrol has been searching for Bijou's whereabouts. They found an entrance generated by magic under the divine tree, and the severely injured Bijou seemed to have escaped into it.

The adventurer was entrusted to enter the entrance for investigation and accidentally saved the young girl Yzma, who was besieged by the green snakes. The world connected by this entrance is very similar to Wasteland, but there are some differences. Through conversation with Yzma, the adventurer learned that Maple is still alive, and the divine tree is still a seed. The adventurer wanted to continue gathering clues to confirm the situation in this world, but heard a cold voice warning.

The adventurer and Yzma went to check the divine tree together and reunited with Ulo, but he didn't recognize them. Through conversation with Ulo, the adventurer learned that this world was the Wasteland of a thousand years ago - Maple Leaf Faramita.

Ulo was worried about the divine tree not being able to grow, so the adventurer suggested him to play the flute based on his experience. The divine tree grew in the sound of the flute, and just as Ulo was about to thank the adventurer, Maple Leaf Faramita suddenly became filled with demonic energy, and the demons went mad one after another. Ulo entrusted the adventurer with the task of solving the demon problem and hurriedly went to discuss countermeasures with Gunn.

2847517: The balance value increase and decrease rules are as follows:
2847518: ① Whenever a monster takes damage, the balance bar increases, and the increase value is proportional to the damage value;
2847519: ② Whenever a monster is hit by the Sword of the Kingdom during the chant of the Corrupted Breath, the balance bar increases significantly;
2847520: 3) Whenever a monster deals damage to an adventurer, the balance bar decays, and the decay value is proportional to the damage value.
2847521: During the "Break" state, the balance value of the monster will continue to decrease and will not increase. At the same time, the monster cannot perform any actions. When the balance value is reduced to 0, the monster will be released from the "Break" state and return to normal.

2857151:
I. Participation Rules
1. Competition Time:
You can sign up for the competition during the specific cup opening time. Within a week of the cup opening, Monday to Friday is the team building time. Team registration starts at 5 am on Friday, ends at 24:00, and the official competition begins at 20:00 on Saturday.
2. Registration Rules:
The team must have a full roster of 12 members, and after all members have clicked the confirm button, the team leader can proceed with the registration.
3. Competition Rules:
①. A maximum of 32 teams can enroll in the cup, and after registration, the participating qualifications will be determined based on the total 6-on-6 scores of all team members. Teams with higher total scores will be given priority for participation.
②. Before the official start of the competition on Saturday, team members must be online and form a team. The team leader must click "Start Match" to confirm participation in the competition 15 minutes prior (19:45-20:00). Teams not clicking "Start Match" within the specified 15 minutes will be considered forfeiting the competition; The match cannot be performed when there are non-registered team members in the team, when there are offline members in the team, and when there are fewer than seven members in the team.
③. After the team leader clicks "Start Match", the team will enter the matching state. If the team wins in the competition, there is no need to click the match again, and the system will automatically enter the matching state. However, if there are members who leave the team resulting in fewer than seven members in the One Dan, the matching state will be canceled, and the team will not be able to continue participating in the competition. Please ensure that the team has at least seven members and is always in the matching state; The matching state will also be canceled if team members change professions during the match.

II. Competition Mode
1. After the registration ends, the registered teams will be randomly grouped. The competition mode is a single-elimination system.
2. If one side of the competition doesn't match, the other side wins automatically. If neither side matches, one side will be randomly chosen as the winner.

III. Special Situations
1. After the official start of the competition, if there are special situations such as server fluctuations causing a round of competition to not start normally, that round will be automatically postponed to the next round's competition time in half an hour. Participating teams should pay attention to system announcements and the remaining match time displayed in-game.
2. If a match is not judged for a winning or losing state as expected, the match results will be deemed void, and the match will be automatically rescheduled for half an hour later in the next round of competition time. The remaining teams don't need to compete again and will be delayed by one round.
3. If the postponement time is too long due to special reasons, and the remaining matches start at 23:30 or later, the remaining competitions will be automatically postponed to the next Saturday at 20:00. Participating teams should pay attention to system announcements and prepare for the competition next week.

【Copy Levels】
Base level 160 unlocks copies. Copies are divided into "Warrior" and "Elite" difficulties. Clearing an Elite level will automatically unlock the corresponding Warrior level, but clearing a Warrior level will not unlock the corresponding Elite level.
【Copy Gameplay】
Adventurers fight monsters on airships to protect supplies flying to the end and clear all monsters to pass the copies. The shorter the time to clear the copies, the higher the settlement score, and the faster the airship speed when clearing monsters.
Dynamo: After being destroyed, it will limit the airship's maximum speed and needs to be repaired nearby.
Supplies: When stolen by Stin, they will escape from both sides of the deck and deduct the settlement score.
Laser: When triggered, it will cause a stun effect on monsters.
Cannon: Can be used to attack monsters flying in the air.
Note: Dynamo, Laser, and Cannon all have cooldown times.
Every time you revive in a copy battle, the settlement score will be deducted.
Each week, copies will randomly add two affix effects to the MVP and Mini. Click on the skill icon on the monster display to view the details.
【Reward Rules】
After clearing the copy, visit the chest to receive the reward. The reward will be deducted from the weekly reward limit and gameplay duration (or battle duration). The first reward on an account each week does not consume duration. The total score of the cleared copy will determine the evaluation, which affects the amount of reward received:
5200 points and above will receive an SSS rating, 110% reward, and unlock challenge level difficulty+3;
4000 points and above will receive an SS rating, 100% reward, and unlock challenge level difficulty+2;
1800 points and above will receive an S rating, 80% reward, and unlock challenge level difficulty+1;
Below 1800 points will receive an A rating, 50% reward, and can't unlock subsequent levels;
Copy rewards are limited to 5 times per account per week, and the reward limit is refreshed at 5 am every Monday.
After clearing a difficulty and receiving a rating each week, the sweep function of that difficulty can be unlocked. Click Sweep to receive rewards based on the account's highest rating in that difficulty during the week. The sweep function resets at 5 am every Monday.
【Fatal Protection Limit】 Airships are surrounded by monster legions, and the "Fatal Protection" effect prepared by adventurers will only take effect once in a battle.
Note: Holy Crystal has a chance to drop.

1. The White Knights' Prestige can be obtained in various ways, such as completing the Tears of the Ancient City adventure quest, unlocking the Jump Tower, opening the treasure chest guarded by elite monsters, etc. Adventurer Dodo, please explore the Tears of the Ancient City map~

2. There is an upper limit for The White Knights' Prestige, which is related to your current White Knight rank; when you reach the current limit, any additional Prestige gained will not be recorded; each time you raise your White Knight rank, the Prestige limit will also increase.

3. Each rank's advancement rewards can only be obtained once and will be sent to the character that reaches the rank first.

4. In the map of Tears of the Ancient City, the wild monsters all have their own White Knight rank. The rank difference between the adventurer and the monster will affect the battle between them, with the following rules: ① For every rank that the monster is above the adventurer, the damage the adventurer deals to the monster is reduced by about 30%, up to 99%; ② When a monster's rank is one level above the adventurer, the damage it deals to the adventurer increases by 100%, and then increases by about 200% for each level beyond that.

5. Many monster camps are scattered throughout the Tears of the Ancient City map. Adventurers only need to join the battle with the monsters in the camp. After the battle, they will have the chance to open the elite treasure chest guarded by the monsters, but if they do not participate in the battle, they will not be able to receive the treasure chest rewards when it ends.

6. Each elite treasure chest can only be opened once per day by the same character, and there are additional rewards for the first opening.

A mini game exclusively for RO players! 
If you have enough knowledge about RO monsters, come and play the mini game Monster Q&A! 
In this game, you need to answer questions about the monsters of each round within the time limit. 
Questions include monsters' color, number of feet, elemental attribute, and race. 
If you succeed in more than half of the total rounds of one stage, you win; otherwise, you lose. 
For each successful round, you have a chance of getting instant completion counts or extra time. Tap the Instant Completion button to win this round and advance to the next round. 
Note: If a question contains A and B, only those satisfy both are counted. If a question contains A or B, any monster that satisfies one of them are counted. If a monster satisfies both, it can't be counted twice. 
Players are rewarded only on their first stage clearance. 
Moreover, each character may play this game 5 times per day at most. A victory in any normal stage doesn't consume your counts while 1 attempt will be consumed in the challenge mode. Your max counts reset the next day at 5 o'clock.
302770:

If you are a master photographer, come and try the mini game Monster Photography! 
In this game, you need to take pictures of the correct number based on the monsters in the field of each round within the time limit. 
If you succeed in more than half of the total rounds of one stage, you win; otherwise, you lose. 
For each successful round, you have a chance of getting instant completion counts or extra time. Tap the Instant Completion button to win this round and advance to the next round. 
Players are rewarded only on their first stage clearance. 
Note: This game also features 3 skills, instant kill attack, small-range knock-back attack, and reset this round's monsters, for players to adjust the location of monsters. 
Moreover, each character may play this game 5 times per day at most. A victory in any normal stage doesn't consume your counts while 1 attempt will be consumed in the challenge mode. Your max counts reset the next day at 5 o'clock.

A mini game exclusively for RO players! 
If you have enough knowledge about RO cards and a good memory, come and try the mini game Card Match! 
In this game, you need to match all cards' front, back and effect within the time limit. 
For each successful round, you have a chance of getting hints or extra time. Tap the Hint button to flip over a matched pair of cards. 
Note: A successful match rewards extra time while an error might result in a punishment (If the wrongly matched cards are both flipped for the first time, no time will be deducted). 
Players are rewarded only on their first stage clearance.

Match Rules:
Each game lasts for 5 minutes.
Each game allows up to 30 players. Players may enter the match as an individual.
There's a 120-second matching time before each game. Matching will be cancelled automatically if it times out.
 After entering, athletes need to choose a monster to transform into within 10 seconds before starting the game. 
Each monster's stats and skills are different. Please choose carefully. 
The item Purple Apple can be found on the match ground. Pick it up to earn 7 Sports Event Sports Points. 
A small amount of new Golden Apple will emerge every 2 minutes. Pick it up to earn 25 Sports Event Sports Points. 
Attack other players and reach 7,000 points of damage to earn 1 Sports Point. 
You'll lose some sports points if knocked out by other players. 
Earn 3 Sports Points for each player you have knocked out. 
At the end of each game, Sports Points will be settled and ranked. The top 3 players will be rewarded: Honor of Sports - Sun, Honor of Sports - Moon, and Honor of Sports - Star. 
Sports Points can be used to exchange for other item rewards. 
Up to 500 Sports Points can be earned per day. 
Leaving in the middle of a game will result in the loss of Sports Points. Each game's Sports Points are calculated separately. 
In case of disconnection during a game, reconnect within 1 minute to return to the game and retain Sports Points. 
No items are allowed during the game.

312304:
A Star Bridge shard fallen from the sky with mighty impacting force opened up a rift that connected Payon Forest to the world of Spirits. Manipulated Epic Spirits and monsters wrapped in the dark mist unfolded a crisis in Midgard... 
As the Epic Spirits were defeated and purified, a new wave began surging on this recovering continent. Oracle Arcana arrived from the rift. Another war was to break out over the scattered Star Bridge shards. 

Fantasy Domain - Payon Forest Guide: 
Players must reach Lv. 12 to enter the battlefield. 
Players can only access the battlefield as part of a team. Only team leaders may perform the match. 
Leave the team in the Dungeon will result in exiting the battlefield. 
Each battlefield may accommodate up to 6 adventurers. 
Each battle may last up to 10 minutes. After, players will be teleported to Prontera West Gate. 
Adventurers win when all Monsters and Arcana clones on the battlefield are killed. 
Each adventurer may obtain the victory reward Otherworld Trophy twice per day. After, they may still access but no rewards will be granted. (Account limited) 
Adventurers can earn Rainbow Light Shards on the battlefield, which can be used to exchange for combat supplies.

Silent Glow - Mjolnir Mountains introduction: 
※Adventurers must reach Lv.12 to enter the battlefield. 
※Each adventurer must be in a team to enter the battlefield, and only the captain can process the matching. 
※Leaving the team during the instance will regarded as leaving the battlefield. 
※A maximum of 6 adventurers can be entered on each battlefield. 
※The maximum duration of each battle is 10 minutes. If the time exceeded, players will be teleported to Prontera West Gate. 
※Adventurers can only win by killing all Monsters and Epic Spirits on the battlefield. 
※Each adventurer can obtain up to two battlefield victory rewards - "Valkyrie's Bliss" every day. You can still enter the battlefield but cannot get rewards after receiving the reword 2 times. (Account limited)
※Adventurers can kill Monsters on the battlefield to obtain "Rainbow Light Shards", which can be used to exchange for battle supplies. 
※After winning the battle, you can use "Renovatio Breath" to purify the Epic Spirits, and get "Big Cat Voucher·Feast" after use. Epic Spirits who have been purified have the opportunity to help adventurers in the subsequent battles.

3289598:
Distant ancient city sent out cries for help, and adventurers here met Oscar, the time-space dragon who claimed to maintain the order of time and space. He told the adventurers that the space-time was collapsing centered around the ancient city, all because someone changed history. As Wind of Fate, adventurers must stop this. So Oscar took the adventurers back three hundred years ago to help King Schmidt of Rune, putting time-space back on the right track.

Upon returning to the past, the adventurer met Schmidt, who was in high spirits, fighting against the monsters in the dark space. The adventurer fought alongside Schmidt, who told the adventurer that he was originally hosting a military parade, and suddenly appeared here, not knowing how much time had passed. At the same time, Schmidt noticed a mysterious long sword under the adventurer's feet, which was the Kingdom Sword recorded in the royal secret record, the sword of Tristan the founding king of Rune! Schmidt generously gifted the sword to the adventurer and taught him how to use it. The fog lifted, and the two were able to return to the outskirts of Glast Heim. Schmidt, unable to contain his excitement, introduced the adventurer to Glast Heim, showcasing its technology. They even created a warp tower that could transmit instantaneously. However, as they advanced, Schmidt discovered terrible monsters around Glast Heim, led by the Dark Legion of Himmelmez.

In a hurry, Schmidt took the adventurer to the Imperial outpost to find the captain of the vanguard, Feisha, and learn the situation. The Dark Monsters in the Dragon Castle, the abandoned village, and the severely injured Knights all intensified Schmidt's ominous premonitions. After saving the Knights with secret medicine, he decided to release a signal flare to call for reinforcements from the "White Star." The flare attracted more monsters, and Himmelmez appeared before Schmidt, repeatedly asking him where "that thing" was. Schmidt remained silent, and the injured Knights were infected by Himmelmez' cursed orbs, emitting dark energy and pouncing on Schmidt and the adventurer.

As the monsters kept on coming, Schmidt and the adventurer retreated on Peco Peco, eventually reaching the Imperial outpost, where Feisha was. However, what awaited Schmidt was Feisha's attack. It turned out that after Schmidt disappeared from the military parade, the Dark Legion had launched a large-scale attack at the same time. Rumors spread that Schmidt had summoned the forbidden power and brought monsters. Feisha and the people misunderstood him. Believing Schmidt after probing, Feisha apologized for his suspicion. Schmidt magnanimously forgave him. Just then, Heinrich, the empire's top beauty and its Grand Commander "White Star," arrived. The commander, silent and cold in the eyes of outsiders, never doubted Schmidt but was angry at his recklessness, cursing him through gritted teeth.

Schmidt told his story and introduced the adventurer to Heinrich. After a strict examination, Heinrich awarded the adventurer a medal, making him a glorious Knight. To resist the Dark Legion, the adventurer helped Feisha reorganize the Knight team. After consulting with Schmidt and Heinrich, the two decided to retreat the front line to defend the altar, using the power of the altar to repulse the Dark Legion. But before that, a temporary medical station in the Dragon Bone area needs to be evacuated.

Upon arriving at the medical station, the adventurer followed Schmidt to meet Dr. Edelon, the royal doctor. He was researching a cure for the infection but lacked enough samples and materials due to a shortage of manpower. The adventurer and Schmidt risked their lives to remove the dragon's scales, and Dr. Edelon finally developed the Water of Life. Just as they were celebrating, Himmelmez appeared and told Schmidt that the infection was irreversible and all efforts were in vain unless Schmidt could tell her the location of "that thing." Schmidt remained silent, and Himmelmez threatened him by infecting more Knights. Schmidt had no choice but to use the sword to end the Knights' pain, causing the people to grow increasingly dissatisfied, accusing Schmidt of being a Tyrant. But Schmidt didn't argue and protected the people at the critical moment, ensuring the safe relocation of the medical team.

Finally, the vanguard and the medical team gathered at the Guardian Altar. The adventurer helped Feisha repair the altar, and Heinrich asked Schmidt to stay in a safe area. Not wanting to be a monarch who only gave orders, Schmidt sneaked out and activated the altar's switch with the adventurer. As the three switches were fully activated, a loud noise came from the distance. Schmidt and the adventurer rushed over to see several Angry Half-Dragons. They blamed humans for destroying their homes and went on a rampage. Although the half-dragons were quickly defeated by the adventurer and Schmidt, the surroundings were in ruins, and an old man and his grandson were buried beneath. The falling rocks threatened to crush them, and the Knights had to choose to save only one. Would it be the old man or the young child? Schmidt had to make a choice, and this choice would change the future.

The adventurer's suggestion was adopted by Schmidt, and Feisha praised the adventurer's decisiveness. After resolving the incident, the group officially activated the Guardian Altar. The Dark Legion attacked, and Himmelmez was severely injured by the barrier of the altar! Just as everyone was cheering, a dense array of cursed orbs emerged from Himmelmez' body, hitting the fighting Knights, whose life forces were absorbed by Himmelmez. Her injuries recovered in an instant, and the Knights turned into terrifying corrupt monsters, their swords pointed at their former allies. Faced with the immortal monster Himmelmez, everyone could only try to flee to the royal city. Himmelmez pursued relentlessly, catching up with the group in the throne room and releasing a fatal blow. At the crucial moment, the adventurer blocked Himmelmez' attack, allowing Himmelmez to realize that the adventurer did not belong to this timeline. Just as she was about to probe further, a beam of light shot up into the sky from behind the two thrones.

Himmelmez laughed maniacally with excitement, shouting "found it" while turning into a shadow and slipping through the cracks into the gate's back. Finally, Schmidt told the adventurer that behind the two thrones was the key to saving the ancient city - Alice, Himmelmez' target. To open the door, they needed to gather six Knight captains to sit on the thrones, which Schmidt believed would be the secret weapon to save Glast Heim. Under his watch, Feisha and two other Knight captains sat on the thrones.

After the Glast Alliance Army had been stationed, the Adventurer volunteered to go to Glast Heim to assist the Alliance. The moment he arrived at Glast Heim, he learned that the soul of Laurell Weinder the mage apprentice was abducted by Dark Lord and there'd been no news about him!
During his investigation, the Adventurer found that the Dark Lord and his subordinate Dark Illusion fed on souls. They usually kept countless incomplete souls sealed away at Glast Heim.
3352533:
the Adventurer went to the location where the magic fluctuation disappeared, and found the wicked priests and high priests performing some evil ritual, which was for Dark Illusion!
The Adventurer and everyone else managed to stop the ritual designed for Dark Illusion, and unlocked the teleportation tunnel to Glast Heim Cemetery for Lisa.
The enraged Dark Illusion tried to seize the Adventurer's soul! He almost succeeded, but the Adventurer escaped with the help of Reyen and Lisa...
After a thorough investigation and fully prepared, the Adventurer entered an evil dream based on the memories of Laurell Weinder with the help of Morgan the mage.
Thanks to the Adventurer's desperate efforts, Laurell Weinder's sleeping soul was woken. With the help of the heroes, the alliance managed to rescue Laurell Weinder and defeat Dark Lord as well as its subordinates.
Although the crisis at Glast Heim was far from its end, and the alliance still needed to be stationed at Glast Heim to protect the kingdom, this battle was undoubtedly a remarkable victory that greatly inspired the brave soldiers. The justice in them would never fade...
3352534:
It had been a while, but the unconscious Magaleta was not waking, and Seyren's treatment didn't seem to help. He continued to seek methods, and fortunately found Doctor Duke of the laboratory at the clinic. He made a deal with Duke to check on Magaleta. To the Adventurer and Seyren's surprise, Magaleta was caught in a nightmare. To wake Magaleta up, the Adventurer entered Magaleta's dream without hesitation.
The result was satisfactory: Magaleta woke up in one piece. After bidding Doctor Duke farewell, the crew went on exploring the second floor of the underground laboratory, and met Peynaud the ventriloquist, who was confined here as an experiment subject, and his teddy bear companion Hence. Peynaud's condition wasn't good, but luckily, Mr. and Mrs. Badger were also there, and they told the crew a method to suppress the mutation temporarily.
To everyone's joy, Hence the teddy bear knew where Deeven and the others were. To save them, Seyren and the Adventurer decided to free Peynaud and Hence from the jail first. When they were looking for the key, Magaleta was caught in another nightmare. This time, Seyren opted to enter her dream with the Adventurer to find the cause. When Magaleta woke up, the others found in horror that her dream had come true.
The toxic gas worsened the Badger couple's mutation. Hence accidentally sang their love song, which restored their consciousness. However, more trouble was still on the way. Peynaud started to attack his allies. To relieve his pain, Magaleta used Heal, which led to Peynaud's disappearance. To make things worse, the Badger couple also vanished after their last performance.
The crew was upset, but had also grown more determined to save their companions. Following Lili's hint, the Adventurer found out how his companions disappeared from a video tape, but before the crew could rejoice, they were abducted by Wolfchev the culprit's subordinates to his base.
There, they found missing members such as Cenia, who were already controlled by Wolfchev and were about to attack Seyren and the Adventurer unconsciously. Just then, they were woken up by the Wing of Secret badge, and the team of six finally reunited. But the joy wouldn't last long. Since Wolfchev was nowhere to be found, they were still in a dangerous situation.
3352535:
Prince Nait's untimely death plunged the entire Midgards Kingdom into grief.
The Adventurer, Agnes, and some others were invited to the prince's memorial service. There, they noticed that the sight of a certain someone's back and the way she turned around were familiar. It came to Agnes that the crying woman in the foreseeing dream was probably Queen Catharine. If so, Catharine might be able to answer her question: Who was the person in the dream that was going to die?
The Adventurer's crew thus found the queen in the garden, along with Ernst the minstrel, who had grown increasingly close to the queen. The two's suggestive exchanges made the rumor that "Ernst the minstrel was actually the queen's lover" even more convincing. Frank the reporter attempted to take a photo of the two together, but accidentally exposed himself and the Adventurer's crew in front of everybody.
Before the angry queen could condemn them, Ian Walter, prime minister of the former king and patriarch of a royal family among the Seven Royals that engaged in maritime trade, showed up in the garden together with his sons Isenhardt and Isenhour. Ian had always considered the flirting of the queen and the minstrel an eyesore, and seeing it at this moment enraged him even more. Drunk, Ian went into a verbal fight with the minstrel. The others only managed to separate Ian from the queen and the minstrel with the help of the Adventurer. The queen left the garden furious, rendering it impossible for the Adventurer's crew to discuss the foreseeing dream with her.
Just when the crew was feeling down, Isenhardt Walter told Ernst and the Adventurer's crew that his father's rudeness was a result of alcohol abuse grieving the prince's death. Ian Walter was originally going to invite Her Majesty to his birthday party to cheer her up and help her recover from the loss of her son. To do so, Ian even ordered subordinates to gift his family's precious golden-stringed harp to Ernst, so that he could play for Her Majesty.
Isenhardt's sincere apology cooled everyone off. As Isenhardt was Ernst's only friend in the palace, Ernst said that he would not turn down his invitation. As for the Adventurer's crew, they considered the birthday banquet a chance to meet the queen again, so they also accepted.
Ian Walter's birthday banquet was held as planned. The royal members were all present, laughing and chatting, as if no death happened only a few days ago. Ian told all the participants that Ernst the minstrel was going to perform with the golden-stringed harp, a treasure of the Walter family. Hardly had he finished when Ernst was heard screaming in the green room. Everyone rushed over, only to find puddles of blood on the green room floor: Ian Walter's favorite son, the humble and gentle Isenhardt, was lying on the floor, a dagger in his chest. Beside him lay a stranger.
Ian, who lost his beloved son on his birthday, forbade anyone to leave, whatever their excuse. Her Majesty ordered the Adventurer's crew to join Karl the forensic pathologist in investigating the scene, hoping to reveal the truth immediately.
Ernst, a witness, testified that the unknown victim was the murderer of Isenhardt, and he killed himself by taking poison after murdering Isenhardt. However, nobody knew the murderer or why he killed Isenhardt.
During the investigation of the scene, the Adventurer accidentally found that the dagger used to stab Isenhardt belonged to Helmut, Agnes's elder brother. Helmut insisted that he had lost his dagger, but refused to reveal more details. Because Martin the guard captain also testified against Helmut, Helmut became the prime suspect of Isenhardt's murder, and the queen had to order that Helmut be taken into custody.
However, Helmut and Isenhardt were never enemies, so Agnes didn't believe that her brother was the culprit. She requested the Adventurer and Nihil to accompany her to the dungeon where her brother was imprisoned, trying to find out who was framing Helmut and the Reaganfelg family. 
The sun had hardly risen when the Adventurer's crew went to the dungeon to meet Helmut. When they asked about the dagger, Helmut obviously lied. The Adventurer proved Helmut's words to be false with the evident he gathered, and found the reason why Helmut was unwilling to say why he lost the dagger: He lost the Mandrake, a precious herb he was ordered to escort, and wanted to make up for it before anyone found out. However, he was deceived by a black market merchant. Instead of getting the medicine, he even lost the dagger he always carried around.
Although they now knew the truth, they still lacked a way to prove Helmut's innocence, unless they could catch Andrew, the soldier who stole the Mandrake, and make him testify. Helmut told the Adventurer that his good friend, Dona the herb merchant might be of help.
At Dona's residence, the Adventurer really found a proof of Helmut losing the dagger before the case happened. Besides, the crew also found that Andrew stole the Mandrake to save his gravely-sick child.
Now that they had got all the evidence needed, the Adventurer's crew was going to leave, when they realized that Andrew seemed to know quite a lot about the Walters' private matters. Suspicious, the Adventurer showed a piece of evidence at the site of murder to Andrew's wife, and she recognized it as Andrew's belonging. Could it be that the Adventurer's crew had accidentally identified the murderer? But if this was the truth, who was the instigator behind the scenes?
The trial was held at the Room of Throne as planned, during which Helmut and Isenhour had a fierce verbal fight. The Adventurer's crew presented the evidence they collected and proved Helmut's innocence. The audience also learned that Isenhardt's murderer was Andrew, the thief that stole the Mandrake Helmut was escorting. However, the reason why he murdered Isenhardt remained unknown.
Still, one thing was for sure: Many items Andrew carried indicated that he was related to Ian Walter. The Adventurer's crew thus made a wild guess: To give his wife and daughter a better life, Andrew obeyed Ian's order to kill Isenhardt Walter and commit suicide afterwards.
The theory enraged the Walters. None of the royal members believed that Ian would kill his beloved son either. Just when the two sides were arguing, Pavel, the butler of the Walters, claimed that he was Isenhardt's true murderer, and asked the queen to put him in prison.
Of course, it convinced nobody, but it didn't seem to bother the queen. According to her, some matters could be settled as long as there was a conclusion. Recalling what Pavel said to the queen before going to prison and the queen's strange reaction, the Adventurer's crew decided to continue the investigation and find the truth, so that no one would be wronged and Isenhardt's death would not remain unsolved.
The Adventurer's crew sorted through the evidence they had again and realized that Walter's original target was probably Ernst the minstrel instead of Isenhardt. Walter used the golden-stringed harp as a mark and asked Andrew to kill the person who was carrying the harp at the banquet. However, the harp unexpectedly went back to Isenhardt, causing Isenhardt to be killed by mistake.
If so, why would Walter take such risks to kill Ernst, a sheer court minstrel? Could it be that Ernst the minstrel had a second identity?
With this theory, the Adventurer's crew went to Ernst, but Ernst, who was usually gentle and weak, refused to answer. The investigation reached a deadlock. Then, following Karl the forensic pathologist's hints, the Adventurer found some proofs in the storeroom that the minstrel suffered from old arm injuries and had to take painkillers over long terms. Coincidentally, the late Prince Nait had scars at the same place.
Then, the Adventurer read the queen's secret diary in her bedroom and found words seemingly written by Ernst that almost proved Ernst's identity. Agnes and Nihil thought it was time to have a talk with Ernst.
However, they didn't know that Ernst was expecting their arrival and hoping that the Adventurer could make a crucial decision for him.
Just when the Adventurer's crew was going to confront Ernst, Karl brought another important piece of news: He took great risks to open Prince Nait's coffin, and found no scar on the late prince.
So far, with the help of the others, the Adventurer had finally broken all of Ernst's heart locks and reached the truth: He was actually the real son of King Tristan George and Queen Catharine. To destroy the contract between the Seven Royals and secure the throne for his own family, Tristan forced Ernst to move out of the Eternal Palace and away from his biological mother, and assume the identity of a minstrel, and more importantly, as a tool to carry out his plan.
Ernst thought that he had accepted his fate, but he didn't expect it to cause his friend's death. More determined than his fragile appearance might suggest, Ernst said that he didn't want to go on living like this. He thus asked the Adventurer to summon everyone, and announced that he was the real prince, in order to honor his friend, be his true self, and protect his mother from his father's oppression.
However, just then, Ian and Isenhour Walter arrived, and demanded that Ernst pay for Isenhardt's death. The Adventurer pacified Ian Walter, but unexpectedly found out some more shocking truth from Ian that could never be proved: 
Everyone thought that the murderer killed the wrong person due to the golden-stringed harp being in the wrong hand, but Ian had actually told Andrew what his target looked like, and the golden-stringed harp was just a reference. However, Andrew still got the wrong person. That meant, someone had found out about Ian's scheme and taken advantage of it to kill Isenhardt, one of the most promising candidates to the throne.
"That person will remain behind the scenes and drive the royal families to doom one by one."
Ian left this message and went away. Meanwhile, Agnes foresaw an even more serious "disaster"... The scheme hadn't been thwarted... More problems were on the way.

3358955:
1. Player skills with control effects work differently on monsters with different elements and levels. Please tap the icons to view detailed effects. 
2. The control effects and element mechanics only apply to battles between players and monsters, and cannot be applied to battles between players. 
3. Control resist bar has been added and is located under the MVP/MINI monster HP bar. The resist bar determines whether the monster can be affected by control skills. When players use a control skill on the target, the control resist bar will increase. When the bar is full, the monster will become immune to control effects for some time. 
4. Different control types have different growth rates of the resist bars, which are mainly divided into the following two types: 
Hard control: These effects (such as stunned, frozen, etc.) prevent a monster from dealing damage and interrupt skill casting for some time. They significantly increase the resist bar.
Soft control: These effects (such as slowed, immobilized, etc.) restrict a monster's ability for some time. They slightly increase the resist bar. 
5. Control types in details: 
Hard control effects: stunned, asleep, frozen, petrified, fear, nightmare, smile of Eden, heavy slash, silence, disable attack, cast time increase.
Soft control effects: immobilized, rooted, MOV SPD reduced, MOV SPD cap. 
6. Element resist bar has been added and is located near the MVP/MINI monster element icon. This resist bar determines whether the monster can be affected by element change skills. When players use an element change skill on the target, the element resist bar will increase. When the bar is full, the monster will negate element change for some time. This state can be viewed at the type displayed to the bottom left of the monster avatar.
7. Poisoned, bleeding, burning and other debuffs and skills that deal a percentage of HP as damage now work on all monsters. When applied to MVP/MINI monsters, these effects will cause the monsters to lose a fixed amount of HP instead.
