42640022:
【Dungeon Process】  
Adventurers must pass through five main landmarks along the route: Fossil Plaza, Explorer Beach, Chess Knights' Statue Cluster, Battlefield Ruins, and Warrior Battle Group Statue Cluster. They need to continuously defeat powerful monsters to uncover the source of the anomalies on Explorer Island.  

【Progress Save】  
When adventurers clear a main landmark within Explorer Island, their progress in the dungeon will be recorded. Dungeon progress resets at 5 AM every Monday. If adventurers enter the dungeon multiple times within the same week, the progress starts from the team leader's state, and cleared content will not refresh. 【Note: If adventurers skip intermediate progress under special circumstances and complete later progress first, when entering the dungeon again as a team leader, the skipped progress will not refresh. To obtain rewards for the skipped parts, they can join other players who still have that progress as teammates and clear it again.】  

【Reward Rules】  
There are three powerful MVP monsters within the dungeon, and defeating them earns rewards. Each MVP's loot rewards can only be obtained once per account within a week, with loot refreshing at 5 AM every Monday. Rewards for each MVP are shared across Beginner, Warrior, and Heroic difficulty levels. (For instance: If the reward for the Phantom Dragon MVP on Beginner difficulty is obtained, it cannot be earned again on Warrior or Heroic difficulties.)  
Clearing any difficulty unlocks access to the Raid feature for that difficulty within the same week.  

【Resurrection Rules】  
During battles with MVP monsters, the combat area is restricted, and resurrecting adventurers consumes resurrection attempts. When resurrection attempts run out, adventurers cannot be revived. Each MVP defeat resets the resurrection attempts. Engaging with non-MVP monsters does not consume resurrection attempts.  
Note: Headgear/Fashion items are dropped at random.
42640023:
【Dungeon Process】  
Adventurers must traverse three main areas—Floating Flame Zone, Sea Spirit Ritual, and King’s Glory Ship—defeating powerful monsters along the way to uncover the secrets of Misty Island.  

【Progress Preservation】  
When adventurers pass one of the major landmarks within Misty Island, their dungeon progress is recorded. Dungeon progress resets every Monday at 5 AM. When re-entering the dungeon within the same week, progress starts according to the team leader's saved progress, and cleared sections will not refresh. 【Note: If adventurers skip intermediate progress under special circumstances and complete subsequent sections first, when they re-enter the dungeon as a team leader, the skipped progress will also remain unchanged. To acquire the rewards for skipped sections, adventurers can join another team where that progress is still available and complete it as a member.】;  

【Reward Rules】  
The dungeon contains three powerful MVP monsters that grant rewards upon defeat. Each MVP’s drop reward can be obtained only once per account per week, and drop rewards refresh every Monday at 5 AM. Reward limits are shared across Beginner, Warrior, and Champion difficulties. Clearing any difficulty unlocks the Raid feature for that difficulty during the same week.  

【Revival Rules】  
While battling MVP monsters within the dungeon, the combat area is restricted, and reviving adventurers consumes revival attempts. When revival attempts are exhausted, adventurers can no longer be revived. Each time an MVP monster is defeated, revival attempts are reset. Fighting non-MVP monsters does not consume revival attempts.  
Note: Headgear/Fashion items are dropped based on probability.

1. Within the last 30 days, players can receive a bonus amount equivalent to their recharge amount divided by 10. Each successful gift will deduct the bonus amount equal to the Zeny price of the gifted item.
2. Gifting requires a certain gifting fee, and the higher the value of the gift, the higher the required fee.
3. Only one gift can be sent at a time, and gifts valued below 100,000 Zeny cannot be sent.
4. Gift items are delivered by the Gingerbread Courier. Once the item is delivered, the recipient has five minutes to accept or reject the gift.
5. If the gift fails, the item will be returned to the gifting player's transaction record, and the player can choose to gift it again or retrieve it.
6. The gift button remains available for up to 3 days.
7. Items purchased from the exchange cannot be gifted to friends who were added after the item's purchase time.
8. The gifting function is only available to players who have reached Adven. Class B.

The Nameless and the Adventurer went to Fiery Fort with Oscar the Spacetime Dragon's blessing, only to be stopped by dragon knights of the Red Scale. They had arrived during a crucial moment for the evacuation plan at Shinyscale Highland, and the Red Scale was on high alert. A red-haired girl noticed their blessing and specially allowed them into the fort, where dragons were getting ready to leave Abyss Lake via "Gate of Freedom." Taelia welcomed the two in Queen Letitia's place, because the latter was unwell due to some chronic illness.
The two helped to secure some medication for the weakly Letitia, and finally met her. She turned out to be none other than the red-haired girl from before. Learning about the crisis concerning Yggdrasil, she promised to hand over her Redflame Star once the Gate of Freedom was activated.
To get the Gate of Freedom ready before schedule, the Nameless offered to help. Following available clues, they collected Dragonflame Shinyscales of ancient dragons. However, they then found a fragmented message left by those dragons — "Defeat? The barrier..." The message seemed to be hinting at dragons' destiny of being stuck at Abyss Lake.
When the Nameless gave Shinyscales to Taelia for forging, he was alerted by the tinge of blue in her eyes. Taelia falsely accused the two of thwarting the plan concerning Gate of Freedom, and summoned dragon knights to besiege them.
Despite the Nameless's efforts to stop her, Taelia managed to infuse the Gate of Freedom with her power.
As the Gate of Freedom opened, it drew in lots of dragon civilians, whose power was used to establish a link between Space-time Matrix and Abyss Lake. The Nameless and the Adventurer defeated Taelia, but the Deserter possessing Taelia fled once again.
After Abyss Lake disconnected from Space-time Matrix, Spacetime Dragon's shadow appeared to reveal the truth to all dragons: the Gate of Freedom was a trap the Deserter used to extract their power, so as to connect Space-time Matrix to Abyss Lake. The news was by no means encouraging.
Enraged, the surviving dragons blamed everything on Letitia, and demanded her death. Spacetime Dragon's shadow deducted that the Deserter would seek a new source of power to activate Space-time Matrix now that another trick of his bore no fruit, and the next source of power on his list was probably the missing Letitia.
At the Twilight Throne, everyone saw Letitia sleeping in a dreamcore. In her dream, "Nidhogg" repeated brainwashed her with fake guidance. When the Nameless destroyed all the dreamcores, Letitia's tears scorched the ground. The bewitched queen finally came to her senses. The Nameless and the Adventurer witnessed the entire trick in her dream — taking advantage of Letitia's respect for Nidhogg and care for her subjects, the Deserter pretended to be Nidhogg and asked her to build the Gate of Freedom and lead all the dragons through it.
To amend her mistake and save her beloved subjects, Letitia used the Redflame Star to threaten Spacetime Dragon's shadow into reversing time and reviving the dead dragons. Spacetime Dragon's shadow had to comply. Letitia's weak voice faded into thin air, while her power turned into crimson particles that wrapped around the Gate of Freedom, from which dead dragons emerged to find two objects lying on the throne: the Redflame Star and a dragon egg covered with cracks.
In the end, the Nameless and the Adventurer watered Yggdrasil's roots with Letitia's Redflame Star, which healed the roots partially.
Spacetime Dragon's shadow had to fix errors in time and space caused by Letitia, while the Adventurer and the Nameless embarked on their next journey. They were heading to Animitta Swamp in pursuit of Blackflame Dragon's Blackflame Star.

1. [Echoing Corridor] is a dungeon with randomly generated maps, monsters, and mechanisms, with increasing difficulty at each level. Pets cannot be brought into the dungeon, but Mercenary cats can be taken. Each Mercenary cat counts as a team member, allowing a maximum team of six to challenge the dungeon.  
2. Each level has nine rooms, including: an entrance room, an exit room, two normal monster rooms, two boss monster rooms, one Tarot room, one Shop Room, and one Rest Room.  
3. Adventurers can obtain keys and coins by clearing normal monster rooms and boss monster rooms. When enough keys are collected, players can proceed to the next level via the exit room.  
4. Adventurers can acquire various items during the run to assist in exploration and combat.  
5. In the Tarot room, adventurers can accept guidance from fate. Three Tarot Cards are randomly refreshed each time, and players can spend coins to refresh the card pool. After confirming the card pool, one card is randomly drawn from the three options. Players can spend coins to draw again, but cards already discarded cannot be redrawn. Tarot Cards have a variety of effects, including the following:  
   - Combat card: Engage in combat to obtain a key.  
   - Cost card: Sacrifice beneficial effects to gain a key.  
   - Item card: Gain powerful Tarot artifacts, any excess artifacts are converted into 100 coins.  
6. In the entrance room of each level, adventurers can perform save operations. Saves retain the current level and acquired items. When reloading, the level resets, and the cost of refreshing the shop and Tarot Cards is preserved in the save. Accepted Tarot Cards and their effects cannot be altered. Upon re-entering the Tarot room after reloading, prior saves will activate. There are two types of saves: automatic and manual. Automatic saves occur when entering a new level, overwriting the previous save and cannot be manually deleted. Manual saves allow up to four slots, and new saves will overwrite the oldest ones when full. Each save is valid for up to one week and is automatically cleared every Monday at 5:00.  
7. First-clear rewards: Each account can receive a first-clear reward upon completing a level for the first time by collecting keys and successfully leaving that level. This reward is only granted once per level per account. Weekly rewards: The range of weekly rewards is determined by the account's highest historically cleared level (as of the previous week's data). For every 10 levels, there is a tier (e.g., 1-10 levels, 11-20 levels). If a higher tier is unlocked through newly added levels (e.g., 21-30 levels), the first clear within the new tier still grants rewards based on the highest historical tier from the previous week. If the current week's challenges fall below the highest historical tier (e.g., highest is 20, but only 1-10 are played this week), rewards will be issued based on the actual level cleared.  
8. Monsters possess various affixes, including:  
   - Gaze: Randomly targets a player, releases a countdown death buff upon approaching them, but the buff is removed after the creature's death and a small purification effect occurs.  
   - Corruption: Generates a pool of poison mist around itself whenever hit, dealing percentage damage to players.  
   - Symbiosis: Three Symbiosis monsters spawn together in a room, executing a charge attack on random players. If one Symbiosis monster dies while others remain alive, it will resurrect 5 seconds later.  
   - Concealment: Continuously spawns minions to attack the players while remaining invisible for 60 seconds. The main body must be located and defeated.  
   - Enslaved: Spawns alongside an invisible Rune orb that grants the monster powerful buffs and can resurrect rune beasts.  
   - Sealed: Clears the battlefield at fixed intervals while the monster remains alive.  
   - Light's Blessing: Grants a powerful aura that significantly increases Holy/Water/Fire/Mind/Poison resistance for other monsters in the area.  
   - Shadow's Blessing: Grants a powerful aura that significantly increases Dark/Wind/Earth/Undead/Neutral resistance for other monsters in the area.  
   - Hold Ground: Grants an aura that prevents other monsters from being affected by control effects.  
   - Split: Killing the monster spawns five Porings, which must be eliminated within a time limit; otherwise, they will merge back into a full-health monster.  
   - Words of Death: Upon death, grants powerful buffs to nearby monsters; prioritize killing this one last.  
   - Explosion: Triggers a large area explosion 2 seconds after death.  
   - Web: Sprays webs, reducing the Move Spd of players within a 10-yard range by 50% for 10 seconds.  
   - Arcane: Periodically summons Arcane orbs around itself, dealing explosive AOE damage to players who come into contact.  
   - Curse: Reduces the player's Healing Effect upon attack.  
   - Thorns: Damaging the creature has a chance to stun the attacker.  
   - Bloodlust: Continuously depletes its health to enhance its damage and resistance.  
   - Void: After a 1-second cast, disables the use of skills and items for players in its vicinity for 3 seconds.  
   - Unsighted: Inflicts debuffs on players attacking it, reducing their speed, extending cast times, and lowering resistances.  
   - Evil Armor: Grants an aura that provides super armor and physical resistance to nearby monsters.  
   - Frenzy: Normal attacks apply the frenzy buff to players, with higher stacked layers increasing damage.  
   - Enfeeble: Temporarily disables the target's ability to attack or use skills.  
   - Hawkeye: Grants an aura ensuring 100% accuracy of nearby monsters’ skills.  
   - Fragility: Grants an aura that amplifies damage received by nearby players.  
   - Healing: Restores 30% health of all remaining monsters upon death.  
   - Inflamed: Becomes immune for 3 seconds when health drops below 50%, increasing its damage during this time.  
   - Bounty: Actively flees; killing it drops a large amount of coins.

In the mist of Animitta Swamp, the breath of death feels Shadow-like.

Piles of dragon bones are scattered across the desolate wilderness, resembling remnants of some forbidden ritual. Among these remains wander a group of "living" dragons—void of emotion, stiff in movement, as if their souls had long been extracted.

In this lifeless land, only the young dragon Thor, yearning to join The Black Claw, still carries sparks of hope in his eyes.

Meanwhile, a dragon tribe member identifying himself as Snow seeks help from the protagonist group, claiming that the Blackflame Dragon has been manipulated by Deserter and has begun slaughtering his kin. But as the investigation deepens, a more terrifying truth emerges—the fragments of a soul-transfer instrument in secret pathways, reports on revival fluid, experiment logs... and a contract of cooperation signed between Blackflame Dragon and Deserter.

It turns out that those "slaughtered" dragons were already fallen dragon warriors. Their remains were used to create revival bodies, parasitized by time-space waste, returning as "pseudo-dragons." Once Blackflame Dragon uncovered this deceit, the hunt began—he would use his black flames to purify these desecrated entities.

"We just wanted to go home..." screamed Cedar, the unmasked time-space waste, "just like the dragon tribe wishes to leave Abyss Lake! We aren’t a natural mistake—it is this flawed world that turned us into errors!”

The Nameless faltered for the first time. If deception could create order amidst chaos, could it also deserve acceptance?

Yet Blackflame Dragon’s black flames suddenly swept across the scene, obliterating all the time-space waste. "Your compassion will only pave their path home with more dragon bones!" he mocked coldly within the flames and disappeared into the mist. Despite Blackflame Dragon's accusations, The Nameless refused to remain silent—instead, he decided to follow in his footsteps.

From then on, The Nameless changed. When the adventurers began noticing something unusual, he left behind only a cryptic riddle: "If wisdom is confined by rules defined by the past... then none will escape Abyss Lake."

The trap was set, the prey captured—when Deserter proudly revealed himself, he was unaware that the "Blackflame Dragon" before him was actually The Nameless in disguise, turning Deserter’s own strategy against him.

However, the imprisoned Deserter struck with piercing words, breaking through Blackflame Dragon’s emotional defenses: "What remains of the legacy you protect, The Black Claw? Just a pile of bones and your pitiful Tyrant title."

As a result, Blackflame Dragon fell under Deserter’s control, becoming the most powerful force against the adventurer group.

At the brink of collapse, Thor’s voice pierced through the gloom: "As long as the black flames burn, The Black Claw will rise again!”

Encouraged by Thor, the black flames re-ignited. Blackflame Dragon broke free from Deserter’s grasp, throwing the Blackflame Star toward the protagonist group before turning away, never looking back!

At the edge of Animitta Swamp, new beacons began to ignite.

Now, with three Dragon Stars gathered, Yggdrasil’s life force is slowly reviving. The final answer lies in the Blessed Forest’s depths, where Nidhogg slumbers—what revelation will he bring?

And so, wisdom and deceit are destined to have their ultimate battle.

Exchange Pre-order Rules: 
1.  The exchange pre-order feature is only available during the effective period of the Premium. Once the Premium expires, all current orders will automatically end, and no new orders can be placed. 
2.  Players can search or browse listed items in the exchange to find the desired product for pre-order. After selecting the item and specifying the quantity and other requirements, an order can be created. Currently, up to 4 pre-orders can be active simultaneously, and multiple orders can pre-order the same item. 
3.  Each order lasts for 72 hours. During this period, the system will automatically purchase items that meet the order requirements until the order time expires or the order requirements are fulfilled. 
4.  Pre-order orders will continue to auto-purchase while players are offline. However, for listed items, the system checks them at intervals, which may result in a delay in purchasing the desired item after it is listed. Please understand. 
5.  When an order is created, the system automatically generates a pre-order unit price. This price is a system-recommended price considering the maximum price increase of the target item during the order period. Players are allowed to modify the pre-order unit price but cannot purchase items that exceed the pre-order unit price. 
6.  The system will calculate the total price based on the pre-order unit price and quantity. Players must prepay the required Zeny when creating an order, which will serve as the funding pool for purchasing the target items. 
7.  During the order period, the system will automatically participate in purchasing listed items during their public notice phase. If the purchase fails, the Zeny will automatically return to the funding pool. If the purchase succeeds, the items must be claimed via the transaction record. 
8.  When an order is canceled, all remaining Zeny in the order's funding pool will automatically be refunded to the character's backpack. 
9.  The pre-order feature does not support buying items from stalls. 
10.  When players pre-order or purchase items from the exchange, if the total quantity of pre-ordered items, purchased items, and account-held items exceeds the maximum holding limit, the item cannot be further pre-ordered or purchased from the exchange. The account-held quantity includes items in the backpacks, various warehouses, Adventure Handbook deposits, current Equipment, etc., of all characters under the account. 
11.  The maximum holding limit varies for different items.

1. Prestige of Blue Wing Guard can be obtained through various methods, such as completing The BlueWing Guards quests in the Abyss region, unlocking the Warp Tower, or opening treasure chests guarded by elite monsters for the first time. Adventurers like Dodo are encouraged to explore the map!
2. The advancement rewards for each level of Prestige of Blue Wing Guard can only be received once and will be issued to the first character to reach that level.
3. The map is scattered with numerous monster camps. Adventurers only need to join the battles with the monsters in the camps, and upon conclusion of the battle, they will have an opportunity to open the elite treasure chests guarded by the monsters. However, failing to participate in the battle means no treasure chest rewards can be claimed upon its conclusion.
4. Each elite treasure chest can only be opened once per day by the same character.
5. When adventurers defeat invading otherworldly MVP or Mini monsters at the Space-time Matrix across the Abyss Lake, they will receive corresponding generous rewards. However, the number of rewards claimable each day is limited—once the upper limit is reached, no more rewards can be claimed on that day. Prestige levels, including Prestige of Blue Wing Guard, throughout Abyss Lake will influence the number of rewards obtainable for otherworldly MVPs and Minis in the Space-time Matrix.
6. In addition to the rewards for repelling otherworldly monster leaders, adventurers can also earn an extra purification reward each day upon reaching a certain purification progress level in the Space-time Matrix zone. All Prestige levels throughout Abyss Lake will affect the purification rewards adventurers receive—higher Prestige levels result in more generous purification rewards.
7. Once Prestige levels reach level 4, adventurers can visit 【Valhna】 and pay a certain amount of Zeny to receive the daily rewards from all camps in the Abyss region.
44702213:
1. Red Scale Group Prestige can be obtained through various methods such as completing The Red Scale missions in the Shinyscale Highland area, unlocking the Warp Tower, and opening chests guarded by elite monsters for the first time. Adventurer Dodo is encouraged to explore the map~
2. The progression rewards for each level of Red Scale Group Prestige can only be obtained once and will be granted to the first character to reach that level.
3. Numerous monster camps are scattered across the map. Adventurers simply need to join battles against the monsters within these camps. After the battle ends, there is a chance to open the elite chest they protect. However, if you do not participate in the battle, you cannot claim the chest rewards upon its conclusion.
4. Each elite chest can only be opened once per day by the same character.
5. When adventurers defeat invading MVPs or Mini monsters from other worlds at Space-time Matrix locations around Abyss Lake, they can receive corresponding substantial rewards. However, there is a daily limit on the number of times rewards can be claimed, and once this limit is reached, no rewards can be claimed again for that day. All Prestige levels at Abyss Lake, including Red Scale Group Prestige, influence the number of rewards adventurers can get for defeating MVPs and Mini monsters at the Space-time Matrix.
6. In addition to the rewards for defeating other-world boss monsters, adventurers can earn an additional purification reward by achieving a certain purification progress value in the Space-time Matrix area daily. Prestige levels at Abyss Lake also influence the purification rewards adventurers receive—the higher the Prestige level, the more substantial the purification rewards will be.
7. After reaching Prestige level 4, adventurers can visit 【Med】 and pay a certain amount of Zeny to instantly claim the daily rewards for all camps in the Shinyscale Highland area.

Prestige levels, including Dark Claw Camp Prestige, will affect the number of MVP and Mini rewards adventurers can obtain in the Space-time Matrix.
6. Aside from the rewards for defeating interdimensional monster bosses, adventurers can also earn an additional Renovatio reward upon achieving a certain Purification progress value in the Space-time Matrix area daily. The prestige level of Abyssal Lake will also influence the Renovatio rewards adventurers receive. The higher the prestige level, the more abundant the Renovatio rewards!
7. Once your prestige level reaches Level 4, adventurers can visit Salvatore and pay a certain amount of Zeny to receive daily rewards from all camps in the Animitta Swamp area.

44704773:
[Copy Introduction]
Every midsummer, Gensokyo holds a grand blessing ceremony to gather the "good fortune" energy needed for the new year. This year, to enhance the fun of the "ceremony," the Celebration Committee has specially created the floating "Rainbow Island," allowing Dream City Residents to ride the magic-enhanced "Rainbow Train" through seven Rainbow Gates to gather energy. At the Destination, Pinata representatives will present flowers and gifts. Just as the entire Gensokyo is cheering for this new ceremony, a group of Mischief monsters suddenly occupies Rainbow Island...
Adventurers, please escort Dream City Residents to safely gather energy and reach the Destination!
[Dungeon Rules]
1. Once the dungeon begins, the "Rainbow Train" will depart at regular intervals, while monsters will continuously spawn at the edge of the field. In Beginner difficulty, the "Rainbow Train" departs six times, and Adventurers must successfully escort six trains to the Destination to complete the challenge. In Endless difficulty, the "Rainbow Train" departs continuously, and Adventurers must do their utmost to escort them.
2. The Residents' "Rainbow Train" has health points, and all monsters prioritize attacking the train. In Beginner difficulty, if any train is destroyed by monsters or all Adventurers die, the dungeon challenge fails. In Endless difficulty, the challenge fails if a total of 15 trains are destroyed or all Adventurers die. Upon failure, the dungeon resets after 5 seconds.
3. The more trains successfully reaching the Destination, the stronger the monsters that will appear to cause Mischief.
4. Successfully completing the Beginner difficulty challenge grants rewards. In Endless difficulty, every six Residents escorted to the Destination grants a reward. As the number of successful escorts increases, the number of rewards also increases. Rewards accumulate in a Chest, and Adventurers can claim them after the dungeon challenge ends. Rewards have a daily acquisition limit.
5. In Endless difficulty, the final number of Dream City Residents successfully escorted by Adventurers will be recorded in the leaderboard. If multiple Adventurers escort the same number of Residents, their rankings will be tied. The leaderboard records the top 1,000 Adventurers, with characters under the same account ranked based on the highest escort count.
6. After the event ends, titles will be sent via mail based on rankings.
The titles corresponding to rankings are as follows:
Rank 1: [SSS Class Escort Specialist]
Rank 2–3: [SS Class Escort Specialist]
Rank 4–10: [S Class Escort Specialist]
Rank 11–30: [Class A Escort Specialist]
7. Once the event period ends, the dungeon Entrance will close.

I. Event Information  
1. Event Time: Every Sunday from 14:00-24:00  
2. Event Map: Abyss Lake  
3. Event Cycle: During the event period, 
every 15 minutes a new round of Dragon Apocalypse activity will begin.

II. Participation Method
1. During the event time, 
go to Abyss Lake and use the small map to view areas with different difficulty levels of the Dragon Apocalypse activity.
2. After entering the activity area, 
automatic matching will occur, 
with priority given to instances where your teammates are located.

III. Reward Details
(Note: The weekly reward limit for each type of reward is shared across different difficulty levels of the Dragon Apocalypse activity)
1. Participation Reward: [Time and Space Advent Box]
* At the end of each round of the activity, 
adventurers who participate in combat will receive 1 reward box. 
Accounts are limited to receiving 1 per week.
* Higher activity difficulty will result in richer rewards.

2. Stage Reward: [Time and Space Echo Box]
* For every 10% reduction in the health of the Time-Space Dragon, 
a set of 1 group of reward boxes (3 in total) will drop. 
During this stage, 
adventurers who participate in combat may collect up to 8 groups per account per week, 
totaling 24 boxes.
* Stage rewards have identical content across all difficulty levels of the activity.

3. MVP Reward: [Time and Space Guardian Box]
* The team of adventurers who successfully purifies the Time-Space Dragon and achieves MVP status will receive 1 reward box. 
Accounts are limited to receiving 1 per week.  

* Higher activity difficulty will lead to richer rewards. 
The MVP box from the highest difficulty activity may contain the tradable [Secret Dragon Spine Deed].

Brave adventurers, 
unite your strength to assist The BlueWing Guards and work together to repel the invasion of the Time-Space Dragon!

44707054: Hello Adventurer, I am Jed. I've heard quite a few rumors about you, and I'm very happy to meet you today!
44707056: ...There is indeed something I want to ask for your help with... Last night, there was a large-scale meteor shower at the south gate.
44707057: A particularly bright "star" was witnessed falling into the nearby forest, and at the same time, we detected an unknown Time Rift.
44707058: Please, this is a task that only you can handle! Only you can resolve such an extraordinary incident.
44707060: Alright, but if you change your mind, feel free to come to me anytime.
44707061: Where is it, the "fragments" of the stars...
44707065: Adventurer… Adventurer? Are you also here to find the fragments of the "stars"?
44707067: My name is Finn... After the meteor shower last night, I heard a call from a "star."
44707068: The star said it got "injured" while falling and asked me to come here to search for fragments to help it recover.
44707070: So that's how it is... But I can't leave, I must find the fragments and restore the stars.
44707072: In short... no matter what you say, I won't leave! I'm going to continue searching for the star fragments!
44707074: ...Alright, then let's go this way. The stars "told" me that the location is just ahead.
44707075: What on earth is going on?!
44707076: I don’t know either. Just now, I was watching a meteor shower in Orario, but in the blink of an eye, I'm already here...
44707077: Where is this? I don't recall any city like this existing outside of Orario?
44707078: Be careful, those Monsters are surrounding us again.
44707080: Thank you for your help just now!
44707082: My name is Bell Cranel. The person beside me is Lady Hestia, and this one is Miss Ais.
44707083: So, to summarize... after that meteor shower, we were brought here by the Time Rift, correct?
44707085: We know nothing. If we hadn't met you, we might not have even figured out that we had "traveled through time"...
44707086: What about the fragments of the star? Big brother, big sister, have you seen the fragments of the star?
44707088: Now that I think about it, during the battle just now, I remember seeing something flash by and fall into the grass. I wonder if it's the fragment you're looking for.
44707091: But why have these already defeated Monsters suddenly Revived? And why are they trying to seize the Shards?
44707093: Could it be that these fragments possess some mysterious power we don't know about？Are these Monsters actually trying to monopolize this power？
44707098: Actually, this star calling out to me is named the Wishing Star. It told me that as long as I can restore it, it will grant any wish I have.
44707099: I... I always had a wish, and that's why I... but I didn't know it would attract Monsters. I'm sorry...
44707101: Whether it is our "time travel" or the appearance and resurrection of monsters, it may be connected to that meteor shower and the falling wishing star.
44707102: In other words, if we can learn more about it, we might be able to find a way to return.
44707104: Then I'll trouble you to lead the way, adventurer.
44707107: Don't worry, you just need to follow my instructions and reveal your wishes to the crystal ball at the right moment.
44707108: Rotating myriad stars, please accept the seeker’s request and reveal the path of enlightenment.
44707109: Hmm... Hmm... I understand. The stars have already revealed your fate, and I shall be the one to tell you the outcome.
44707110: Divination has already revealed the result—the child did not lie. The fallen star is indeed called the "Wish Star," and it possesses the ability to grant any wish.
44707111: As a result, its fragments continuously attract those with intense desires, whether humans or monsters, drawing them to its side. The resurrected evil spirits emerge in this way.
44707114: You are special, so you heard its call and formed an extraordinary connection with it.
44707115: "Follow the starlight, restore the stars, fulfill Finn's wish, and the path home will automatically appear." This is the final answer.
44707116: So, as long as we help him gather all the fragments of the wishing star and fulfill his wish, we can return to the original world?
44707117: The result of the divination is as follows, but whether to act on it is up to you.
44707118: There's no need to hesitate about this.
44707119: That's right, and this way we can also help Finn. We have no reason to refuse.

44707122: If you have gathered all the fragments, simply head to Comodo, where everything will come to an end...
44707123: Thank you for bringing us to find the Astrology Cat, adventurer.

【Instance Process】  
The consciousness of the Time-Space Dragon has completely fallen into chaos, fleeing from the Abyssal Lake and wandering among various disordered timelines. A large number of monsters from these chaotic timelines are eroding the will of the Time-Space Dragon. Eliminate them and bring the Time-Space Dragon back to the correct timeline! During the battle, adventurers can absorb the power of defeated monsters to strengthen themselves. Choose this power wisely and traverse the storm of time with your companions!  
【Instance Rules】  
1. After the battle begins, a total of 10 waves of monsters will be summoned within the instance. Defeating all monsters in the current wave within the time limit will trigger the summoning of the next wave. Additionally, the team leader can access "Dragon Summon" to summon the next wave earlier. If the team leader chooses to summon the next wave before completely defeating the current wave, both waves of monsters will appear simultaneously.  
2. Each wave of monsters has a limited extermination time. If adventurers fail to defeat all monsters within the time limit, the challenge will fail. If adventurers defeat all monsters within the time limit or summon the next wave early, the remaining time of the previous wave will be added to the next wave's challenge.  
3. The instance features a special level mechanism—Temporal Energy Level. Adventurers will gain Time-Space Energy by defeating any monsters. Accumulating a certain amount will increase their Temporal Energy Level. Each time the Temporal Energy Level is upgraded, adventurers will receive one Talent Point. By consuming one Talent Point, adventurers can select one of three randomly offered talent skills as a temporary boost within the instance. Time-Space Energy gained by defeating monsters is shared among the team.  
4. Each adventurer can choose up to 4 talent skills. Once the limit is reached, only previously obtained skills will appear randomly. If adventurers select a skill they have already obtained, its skill level will increase by one, up to a maximum of level 10. Each skill level upgrade provides additional effects. Adventurers can abandon a chosen talent skill, but doing so will only return 50% of the Talent Points spent.  
5. Adventurers can view all available talent skills for the instance at the skill chart located at the instance entrance.  
6. If the challenge fails, the instance will reset. The adventurer's Temporal Energy Level will return to zero, and all obtained talent skills will disappear. Both the Temporal Energy Level and talent skills are effective only within the instance.  
7. When adventurers revive within the instance, it consumes revival attempts. Once revival attempts are exhausted, adventurers can no longer be revived. Revival attempts will reset when the instance resets.  
8. Each week, 3 random modifiers will be selected from all available modifiers to apply as weekly modifiers. Monster modifiers only affect the targets specified in their descriptions.  

【Reward Rules】  
1. Completing the instance and opening a treasure chest will randomly grant you a Memory Enhancement reward to strengthen the memory of your currently equipped gear. You can choose one from three randomly provided rewards.  
2. If the selected gear slot does not carry a memory or if the gear's level/breakthrough stage has reached its maximum limit, the reward will automatically convert into materials.  
3. Completion rewards for all difficulties do not consume battle time but share reward attempts. Reward attempts reset weekly. Upon completion, you can only claim rewards for the current difficulty level—it is not backward compatible.

[b]Competition Rules[/b]

1) The GVG Final Battle takes place on Sunday %s.

2) Before the start of the Sunday GVG Final Battle, all Guilds occupying cities are eligible to participate and can enter the GVG Final Battle map 3 minutes prior to the start.


[b]Battlefield Rules[/b]

*Factions

The GVG Final Battle involves four competing Guilds. Each participating Guild acts as an independent faction and cannot form alliances.


*Victory Conditions

1) The first Guild to collect 5 [Crystal Resources] wins immediately.

2) If no Guild collects 5 [Crystal Resources] by the end of the battle, the Guild ranked first in Crystal collection will be declared the winner.


*Crystal Resources

1) The battlefield contains 5 areas that produce Crystal Resources for Guilds to fight over.

[Central Core]: Opens for capture 3 minutes after the battle starts. Capturing it grants 2 Crystals, and losing it will immediately deduct 2 Crystals.

[East Crystal Tower] [West Crystal Tower]: Open for capture 3 minutes after the battle starts. Capturing one grants 1 Crystal, and losing it will immediately deduct 1 Crystal.

[Green Guild Fort] [Blue Guild Fort] [Red Guild Fort] [Purple Guild Fort]: Each is worth 1 Crystal Resource if unbroken. If broken by another Guild, the Crystal is deducted and cannot be repaired.

2) If a Guild's fort is broken, all Guild members will experience Forced Dispel to the Guild platform for Revive upon death on the battlefield for a period of time.


*Capturing Method: The Guild with the highest number of members in the capture area accumulates capture value until the capture progress bar is full, securing the area for that Guild.


*Crystal Shard Resources

1) An MVP spawns approximately every 3 minutes on the upper/lower platforms. The Guild of the Player who delivers the Last Hits to the MVP will receive 1 [Crystal Shard Resource].

2) Collecting 4 Crystal Shards converts into 1 [Crystal Resource] that cannot be stolen.


[b]Reward Rules[/b]

Adventurers who participate for at least 3 minutes will receive rewards during the event settlement.

In the depths of the Blessed Forest, the body of the Primordial Dragon Ned Hoge slumbers beneath the Golden Tree. This Golden Tree, as a projection of Yggdrasil, carries the lingering essence of primordial power and holds unknown potential. Oscar the Spacetime Dragon entrusted an adventurer team to seek guidance from Ned Hoge’s spirit in order to obtain the Star of Life. Upon arrival, however, they discovered that the forest had fallen into Worldline Turbulence, with time thrown into chaos. The guardian, the three-headed dragon Norton, had his temporal powers stolen, driving him into a frenzy. To retrieve Norton’s temporal powers, the adventurer team ventured to the Time Turbulence Recycling Station.

The Nameless witnessed firsthand the anguish of time-space debris being consumed by the turbulent currents. He realized that the so-called “order to eliminate erroneous existence” was, in truth, built on the exile of countless innocents. This ruthless reality was precisely what he once regarded as “rightness.” When Norton’s temporal powers were restored, he regained clarity and, as a guardian, invoked Ned Hoge’s spirit to descend. However, Ned Hoge did not appear, with the adventurers discovering that Ned Hoge’s power had been stolen.

To reclaim Ned Hoge’s powers, Norton sacrificed his life to glimpse into Ned Hoge’s temporal trajectory: her power had been fragmented by the Deserter and injected separately into the Worldline Matrix and the Hogne Sword Tomb. The adventurer team journeyed to these locations to retrieve Ned Hoge’s power. Yet even after reclaiming it fully, her spirit did not manifest.

The Golden Tree began to grow wildly, with its branches producing numerous peculiar fruits. These fruits were filled with the collective will of time-space debris and the schemes of the Deserter. The Nameless inferred that the Deserter had closed the Ancient Tree Gate, severing Yggdrasil’s primordial pull on the Golden Tree. Only through this act could the Golden Tree escape its projection identity, develop independent consciousness, and become the source of a new world.

At the Ancient Tree Gate, the adventurer team discovered that Ned Hoge had imprisoned herself in her disappointment. This despair served as the very source of power that sealed the Ancient Tree Gate. Finally, the adventurers guided Ned Hoge to recall that she was both the starting point and the ultimate destination of life. With this realization, Ned Hoge’s spirit finally appeared, and the Ancient Tree Gate reopened. At this moment, The Nameless proposed a new idea: to fuse the Golden Tree’s tears into Yggdrasil’s root system, enabling the Golden Tree to become an extension of Yggdrasil and support the Time Turbulence Recycling Station. However, the Deserter, enraged by yet another failed plan, challenged The Nameless to war.

At the Ancient Tree Gate, The Nameless recovered his original identity—The Nameless was originally the “wisdom” of the god Loki, while the Deserter was his “cunning.” The two had been part of a single entity, separated due to Loki’s ultimate choice. The Nameless attempted to persuade the Deserter to cooperate, but the latter instinctively resisted after years of judgment by “wisdom.” At this critical moment, time-space debris expressed their longing for home. Touched by their desires, the Deserter finally agreed to collaborate. He personally took up the Golden Tree’s tears, intending to fuse them into Yggdrasil—only to be betrayed by the Golden Tree.

It turned out that the Golden Tree, nourished by the power of cunning, had developed independent consciousness and seized the opportunity to consume the Deserter’s strength. This act gave rise to a multitude of tree spirits, which began to reverse-corrupt Yggdrasil, aiming to replace it. Feeling its primordial essence threatened, Yggdrasil instinctively activated its self-preservation mechanism, sealing off all energy pathways and falling into dormancy. The world trembled, life withered, and time-space became unstable.

The Nameless resolved to save the Deserter by severing the tree spirits’ source of power. However, Oscar the Spacetime Dragon appeared and intervened. He firmly upheld the iron law of time—that time exists as a singular stream and must never be divided. The Nameless, however, argued that order should not be founded upon the sacrifice of innocents. As the two clashed fiercely, The Nameless realized that he and the Deserter must reunite to face this formidable enemy. Thus, wisdom and cunning merged once again—the god Loki was reborn.

The dual Loki and Oscar engaged in a fierce battle, evenly matched until Ned Hoge intervened to mediate the conflict. She acknowledged Loki’s attempt, though Oscar still had concerns about who would sustain the balance of the second timeline. Loki proclaimed that he would traverse both timelines to maintain equilibrium.

In the end, Ned Hoge handed over the Star of Life and fused the Golden Tree’s tears within it, with the adventurer team using them to nurture Yggdrasil’s roots. Golden light radiated as the two trees resonated—no longer was the Golden Tree merely a projection, nor Yggdrasil a solitary master. They became two halves, jointly bearing the weight of the world.

Loki led all time-space debris toward their new homeland; the dragons broke free from their thousand-year chains, reclaiming their freedom.

In the wake of this resolution, the Golden Tree Rift re-emerged—a long and graceful white feline creature appeared, whispering: “The world behind the Golden Tree needs you.” Oscar gazed into the Rift, fully aware that beyond it lay the Sealed Jörmungandr.

The combined power of the two trees had now shaken the final Sealed barrier.

The gears of fate turned once more.

1. The prestige of iris group can be obtained through various methods, such as completing Iris group missions in the Animitta Swamp area, unlocking the Warp Tower, or opening elite guarded treasure chests for the first time. Adventurers like Dodo are encouraged to explore the map~  

2. The advanced rewards for each level of The prestige of iris group can only be claimed once and will be awarded to the first character who reaches that level.  

3. The map is scattered with numerous monster camps. Adventurers simply need to join in combat with the monsters within these camps. After the battle concludes, there will be opportunities to open elite treasure chests guarded by the monsters. However, if the adventurer did not participate in the battle, they will not be able to claim the chest rewards when the battle ends.  

4. Each elite treasure chest can only be opened once per day by the same character.  

5. In various locations around the Abyss lake, adventurers can defeat invading otherworldly MVP or Mini monsters in the Worldline Matrix to earn a corresponding generous reward. However, there is a daily limit on the number of rewards that can be claimed. Once the limit is reached, no further rewards can be collected for that day. All Prestige levels in Abyss lake, including The prestige of iris group, will impact the number of rewards adventurers can obtain for defeating MVPs and Minis in the Worldline Matrix.  

6. Besides the rewards for repelling otherworldly monster leaders, adventurers can also earn additional purification rewards by achieving a certain purification progress level in the Worldline Matrix area daily. The Prestige levels in Abyss lake will also affect these purification rewards—the higher the Prestige level, the more generous the purification rewards will be.  

7. Upon reaching Prestige level 4, adventurers can visit 【Adeline】 and pay a certain amount of Zeny to obtain the daily rewards from all camps in the blessed forest area.

44720120:
★ Guild war starts every Thursday from 13:00-14:00 (Group A) and 20:00-21:00 (Group B). You can enter the battlefield through the preparation camps in each city.
★ The Guild that ultimately occupies the city will receive materials to craft Guild artifacts and qualify for the grand final battle.

1. Battle Lines
★ Guilds are randomly assigned to different battle lines. A Guild can only occupy cities and strongholds within its battle line and can only deal damage to the "Emperium" within its battle line.
★ Adventurers can check the status of different battle lines via [More] - [Guild] - [Guild War Status] interface and can also teleport to different battle lines.
★ Each Guild can only participate in one battle line group per week. Guild leaders can change groups through the battle line relocation function.
★ If a Guild has already participated in a Guild war this week within a battle line group, its members will be considered as having participated, and switching Guilds will not reset participation opportunities.

2. Cities
★ Each battle line has 4 areas, each containing one large, medium, and small city, a total of 12 cities.
★ After a city changes ownership, it enters a 60-second cooldown period during which all attacking adventurers will be removed from the battlefield.
★ Guilds can temporarily occupy multiple cities simultaneously, but can only officially occupy one city during the final city settlement phase.

3. Emperium
★ Each city contains one "Emperium" that can only be damaged by Auto Attacks. The adventurer whose Guild delivers the final blow to the "Emperium" will temporarily occupy the city, becoming the defender.

4. Stronghold Contest
★ Each city has 3 strongholds, initially belonging to the defenders, with neutral strongholds by default in unoccupied cities.
★ When the second stronghold belongs to the defenders, the Emperium is invincible and cannot be damaged.
★ When the second stronghold belongs to the attackers, the Emperium loses its invincibility.
★ When the second stronghold is neutral, the Emperium's invincibility is determined by its last ownership.
★ If the second stronghold of a neutral city has never been occupied by the attackers during the battle, the Emperium remains invincible.
★ If an adventurer dies in the Guild war, they can choose to revive at a stronghold or in the Safe Zone after 15 seconds.

5. Perfect Defense
★ If the Emperium in your city remains undamaged during the 15-minute countdown, it achieves "Perfect Defense," and attackers cannot re-enter that battlefield.
★ If the Emperium is damaged during the process, it must be restored to full health, and the countdown resumes after a 60-second wait.

6. MVP Contest
★ 10 minutes after GVG starts, an MVP [Shadow of Morroc] will be summoned in each large city and can only be damaged by Auto Attacks.
★ The Guild that delivers the final blow to the MVP will receive artifact materials.
★ Adventurers can only deal damage to the MVP within their Guild battle line, and cannot damage it during the city's cooldown period.
★ If "Perfect Defense" is achieved and the MVP has not been defeated, the city will not enter the cooldown period, and attackers can still enter.

7. Guild Mercenaries
★ Guilds can hire up to 20 adventurers as mercenaries, and the hire relationship is only effective during the Guild war.
★ Guild mercenaries are counted as members of the hiring Guild for settlement purposes (excluding season rewards), and their enemy/friend status aligns with the hiring Guild.
★ Hiring relationships cannot be changed from 30 minutes before the Guild war starts until the end of the city settlement phase.
★ During the Guild war, enemy mercenaries are displayed with random names in preparation camps and battlefield maps.
★ Guild artifacts can be allocated to mercenaries but cannot be allocated to external Guild members.
★ Guild mercenaries can only use artifacts during the Guild war and in preparation camps.
★ Guilds cannot hire mercenaries across different battle line groups.
44720121:
[b]1. Season and Rankings:[/b]
★ At the beginning of a new Guild War season, each Guild will be randomly assigned to different battlefronts to compete for city ownership. The occupation status of all cities will be reset to neutral.
★ Each Guild War season lasts for 6 weeks, with rankings determined by the sum of the top 4 scores. The remaining time will be the leisure period, during which points will not be counted in the season scores.
★ When the season begins, Guild Wars of different battlefront groups in the same week are considered as the same match and are included in the ranking scores.

[b]2. Scoring Details:[/b]
★ Defending Cities: If the Emperium in the occupied city before the current Guild War remains intact throughout the war, 1 point will be awarded. Maximum 1 point for this item.
★ Attacking Cities: Any Guild that destroys the Emperium of a large city will earn 4 points. The Guild occupying a small city or a Guild without a city that destroys the Emperium of a medium city will earn 2 points. Maximum 4 points for this item.
★ Perfect Defense: Achieving perfect defense in any of your own cities will earn 2 points. Maximum 2 points for this item.
★ City Occupation: After the city settlement period ends, the Guild occupying a large/medium/small city will earn 8/5/3 points respectively. Maximum 8 points for this item.
★ Continuous Occupation: If a Guild occupies a city both before the Guild War begins and after the city settlement period ends, 2 points will be awarded. Maximum 2 points for this item.
★ MVP Kill: Delivering the final blow to the summoned MVP [Shadow of Morroc] in each large city will earn 3 points. Maximum 12 points for this item.

[b]3. Season Rewards:[/b]
★ Guilds occupying large cities during the season will grant their members a 7-day limited-time season mount reward.
★ Guilds ranked in the top X+1 at the end of the season (X being the number of battlefronts) will grant their members a permanent season mount reward.
★ The Guild ranked first in total season scores will grant its members the Season Champion Trophy reward.
★ Adventurers who joined the Guild at least one week before the last season Guild War match can receive season rewards.

1. [Constellation Tower] is a seasonal dungeon. Once a new season begins, previous seasons can no longer be viewed or challenged, and their rewards can no longer be obtained. Adventurers are advised to participate in time to avoid missing the season.
2. [Constellation Tower] consists of four different towers, each with multiple difficulty levels. The first time you clear a difficulty, you will receive its first-clear reward. First-clear rewards are shared across the account and cannot be obtained again. Other than first-clear rewards, there are no regular rewards.
3. [Constellation Tower] cannot be challenged directly from the dungeon interface. The team leader must go to the corresponding entrance NPC in the Endless Tower area and select a difficulty to begin.
4. [Constellation Tower] contains multiple stages. In addition to defeating all monsters, each stage has a time limit. If a challenge fails, you will continue from the current stage.
5. Each tower grants powerful bonus effects to specific Classes. Details can be viewed in [Blessing Bonus]. When the party includes the designated Blessed Classes and the required number is met, the effects will activate within the tower.
6. After completing all dungeons in a season, Adventurers can synthesize a special seasonal SFX. Once obtained, it can be set in the Back Accessory slot in Transmog and will remain active until the end of the next season or until a new seasonal SFX is obtained. It is used by default in [Constellation Tower], and must be manually set outside the dungeon.
7. When clearing higher difficulty dungeons, you will also receive the rewards for all lower difficulties in the same tower.

45386702:
【Dungeon Process】
After Jörmungandr departs, Aquila replaces it to absorb the energy of heaven and earth for Isgard. However, Bagg controls Aquila within the Airship, monopolizing all the energy. Adventurers must board the airship to defeat Aquila, allowing the energy to return to all living beings in Isgard.
【Reward Rules】
Limited to one reward per account per week, with all difficulty levels sharing the reward count. Rewards reset every Monday at 5:00 AM.
【Revive Rules】
During battles with MVP monsters in the dungeon, the combat area will be restricted, and reviving Adventurers will consume revive counts. Once the revive counts are exhausted, Adventurers can no longer be revived.
【Dungeon Rules】
After the Adventurer begins the battle with the Super Sea Butterfly, Aquila will enter a charging state. A system notification will appear for every 10% charge. If Aquila's charge reaches 100%, it will enter attack mode. When the Super Sea Butterfly is defeated, charging will stop, and the current charge progress will be recorded for this dungeon attempt. If the Adventurers are wiped out while challenging Aquila, the charge progress will not reset, and Aquila's mode will remain unchanged.

45499551:
The Guardian robot summoned by Aquila changes its behavior based on Aquila's mode. 

When Aquila enters defense mode, the Guardian can't attack but transfers energy to Aquila, significantly reducing the damage it takes. Additionally, to avoid electromagnetic interference caused by being too close to Aquila, the Guardian continuously activates its electromagnetic Shield, protecting those behind the Shield from the effects of electromagnetic storms.

When Aquila enters attack mode, the Guardian actively joins the fight. If the Guardian becomes excessively damaged during this period, it will be forced to activate its electromagnetic Shield and simultaneously prepare for Self Destruction.
45499652: To cool down the scorching energy core of Cygnus, the Super Sea Butterfly is designed to create ultra-low temperature Cold Snaps. When the Cold Snap strikes, adventurers must find a sheltered area to avoid being Frozen. (The Icicles left on the field might be a good choice...)

45909873:
The space-time dragon Oscar captures the signal of Ymir's Heart behind the Golden Tree.
Meanwhile, a white cat carrying Lasgand's consciousness crosses the Rift with Cenia's commission seeking help. Oscar deduces that a dramatic change occurred in the snow-covered land of Isgard and entrusts the adventurers to investigate.
Through the Rift, the adventurers arrive in Isgard, where extreme storm gusts obscure the path ahead. The white cat appears and reveals the truth: its body is being refined by former Rekenber researcher Bagg into an imitation of Ymir's Heart, whereas Cenia's consciousness and power are slowly being burnt away as fuel.
After defeating the center of the storm and obtaining the Earth's First Snow, Lasgand forges it into a Snowflake Crown, granting the adventurers passage and an alliance.
Following Lasgand's guidance, the adventurers reach the Frostsilver Fortress, the base of the White Eagle Tribe. Here, the Snowflake Crown's power awakens gradually through trials.
The peace is short-lived—Bagg controls the polluted lower Lugans to launch an attack, aiming to cut off White Eagle Guard reinforcements heading to the front line. After a fierce battle, the polluted lower Lugans do not die but instead transform into snake eggs intertwined with dark energy.
Lasgand temporarily restores his human form to purify them and entrusts the adventurers with their return to the Serpent's Nest. Along the way, Bagg's experimental Lugan creations constantly obstruct their path. Through battles, the resonance between the Snowflake Crown and adventurers deepens, ultimately awakening the dormant Snowflake Diamond. Upon returning to the Serpent's Nest, Lasgand recalls witnessing the atrocities committed by Bagg on his people and, through consciousness connection, senses Cenia's increasingly faint calls—she is being manipulated as a weapon and deployed on the battlefield at Avalanche Boundary.
On the way to the Avalanche Boundary, storms rage like blades. Bagg's controlled Aquila descends, and before the gigantic entity stands the manipulated Cenia. Her attack halts at the last moment, and a light of struggle flashes in her eyes. The next moment, she is forcibly recalled into Aquila and vanishes amidst the storm. The Falcon follows closely, taking away everything and triggering an avalanche that blocks the path forward.
To proceed, Lasgand guides the adventurers to Snowmoon Mirror Lake to find Eternal Ice that can purify darkness. Deep within the lake, Jörmungandr's residual negative emotions engulf them like tides while almost collapsing Lasgand's consciousness. The adventurers submerge into his sea of consciousness and retrieve three consciousness cores teetering on the brink of collapse. Amid the chaos, Cenia's faint remaining consciousness shines like a star, guiding their way.
With Eternal Ice, everyone heads to the ancient Snowfall Sanctuary. Wind Whisper Ice Crystal, Eternal Snowheart, Tear of the Beginning, and Aurora Stardust—four sacred relics gather light, initiating the barrier-breaking ritual. The Holy Light breaks through the avalanche's blockade, opening the road to Bagg's domain.
The White Eagle Tribe's army is ready to march, their battle flags snapping in the wind...

* Rubbing-type Materials: Dragon Bone rubbings are consumed first, and if insufficient, Esoteric Dragon Bone rubbings are used.

45919445:
When the light of the snow-lit altar opened the path to the Frostsnow Plains, the Adventurer and the white cat, Lathgand, finally stepped into this frontier region, the Illusory Snowy Pine Forest. Here, with misty hot springs, fields of snow sugar, and serene pine forests, it seemed like a paradise crafted for weary travelers. However, Lathgand quickly realized that this overly perfect gentleness was a Trap meticulously woven by Bagg. He sought to transform the deepest desires, guilt, and attachments of the Intruders into tangible but false happiness, quietly eroding their will to move forward.
At this moment, Cenia's Illusion appeared gracefully. With her familiar and gentle whispers, she attempted to breach the defenses of the Adventurer's heart, trying to lure out the Snowflake Crown: Deep Chill. In this critical situation, Lathgand had no choice but to temporarily leave his cat form and take on his true form to confront the overwhelming Illusionary power of the Illusory Snowy Pine Forest. Under the guidance of Lathgand’s true form, the Adventurer finally broke free from the Dreamland and personally shattered the Illusions. It was at this moment that the Snowflake Crown evolved into the more powerful form of "Deep Chill." After Lathgand's true form departed, the white cat, Lathgand, continued to accompany the Adventurer, pressing further into the Frostsnow Plains.
Through the mist of the Illusory Snowy Pine Forest, they arrived at the Pilgrim's Sanctuary, the former heart of the Lugarn royal authority. Here, the white cat, Lathgand, unveiled a deeper layer of Bagg's scheme: he was extracting the remnants of power from the past kings at the sacred throne to strengthen the "Replica Yimir's Heart." However, having expended too much in the Illusory Snowy Pine Forest to awaken the Adventurer and combat the Dreamland, Lathgand's white cat form could no longer directly ascend to the sacred throne, nor could it establish a stable link with his true form. To shut down the energy hub on the sacred throne, the Adventurer retrieved the scattered souls of the past kings. Ultimately, with the power of the past kings augmenting him, the white cat, Lathgand, ascended the sacred throne, successfully shutting down the hub and severing the throne's energy supply to the "Replica Yimir's Heart."
To accelerate their offensive against Bagg, the white cat, Lathgand, and the Adventurer followed the massive shed skin left behind by the Great Serpent, Jörmungandr, traversing the Snow Sugar Fields and sliding into the Aurora Lands to destroy the "Eye of Vision," thereby weakening Bagg's surveillance and power network. As the initiator of the "Eye of Vision" project, Rongkoer could not tolerate her research being Destroyed. She harbored an Obsession with logic and a near-fanatical admiration and loyalty to Bagg. She turned each battle into a testing ground for theories, as though using her own life to prove her worth to Bagg.
However, when Rongkoer fell, the Ice Cast Clone of Bagg displayed no mourning whatsoever. His attitude, like the Ice Cast Clone itself, was cold. Confronted with the death of a comrade, Bagg, through the Clone, declared his philosophy to all present—death is the ultimate refinement for a scientist. In his eyes, Rongkoer was merely an inefficient vessel prone to errors; only through death could she evolve into a flawless constant within the database.
After the fierce battle with the Ice Cast Clone of Bagg, the white cat, Lathgand, formally declared war on Bagg: they would soon step into the Ice Bound City and personally bring an end to everything. Meanwhile, the vanguard of the White Eagle Guard had already infiltrated the Ice Bound City in secret, completing the final preparations according to Lathgand's plan to secure valuable time for the impending final assault.
At this point, the Adventurer finally understood the significant gap that still remained between them and Bagg's true form, and that the power of the Snowflake Crown had yet to reach its ultimate state. Thus, Lathgand entrusted the Adventurer with a new mission: to continue honing their strength in Isgalt, allowing the Snowflake Crown to evolve into a form capable of enduring the ultimate showdown. As for himself, he would wait on the Icebound Scale Bridge leading to the Ice Bound City, ready to face the true final battle alongside the Adventurer.
The snowstorm raged on, and the aurora shimmered. The fate of Isgalt was finally being pushed toward an unavoidable conclusion.

45986580:
[Instance Process]
In his early years, Bagg, afflicted by Frostbane due to a failed experiment, sealed the contaminated "past" along with the old research institute and the Frostbane Mammoth into Isgalte. Now that the seal has weakened, adventurers must venture into it to prevent the spread of the calamity.
[Reward Rules]
Limited to 1 reward per account per week. All difficulties share the same reward limit. Drop rewards reset every Monday at 5:00 AM.
[Revival Rules]
During battles with MVP monsters within the dungeon, the combat area will be restricted, and reviving adventurers will consume revival attempts. Once all revival attempts are exhausted, adventurers can no longer be revived.
[Dungeon Rules]
The Frostbane Mammoth wields the power of Frostbane, which can corrode armor and dispel buff energy. The Past Bagg also possesses the power of Frostbane, granting him the ability to alter the terrain. Defeating the Past Bagg will yield rewards.

1. Castle Occupation Rewards
① After the Guild War castle settlement period ends, a certain number of Guild Reward Chests can be opened at Al, the Chest Guardian in the Guild Territory, based on the region and size of the castles occupied by the Guild.
★ A castle is considered continuously occupied if the Guild occupies it both before GVG begins and after the castle settlement period ends.
★ Continuously occupying a castle increases the number of Guild Rewards from that castle, up to a maximum of 3 times.
② When the attacking side destroys the Glorious Crystal, Guild members inside the Glorious Crystal room can receive individual rewards, including a certain number of [Badges of Honor]. These rewards can only be obtained for the first destruction in each Guild War. The smaller the size of the Guild’s original castle and the larger the size of the castle attacked, the greater the rewards.
③ A one-time castle defense reward will be issued based on the largest castle temporarily occupied by the Guild when GVG ends. The reward is doubled for a Perfect Defense. If multiple castles are tied for the largest size, the reward will not be issued repeatedly. The specific amounts are as follows:
★ Occupying a small castle grants [Artifact Material Coin] *150. A Perfect Defense grants [Artifact Material Coin] *300.
★ Occupying a medium castle grants [Artifact Material Coin] *375. A Perfect Defense grants [Artifact Material Coin] *750.
★ Occupying a large castle grants [Artifact Material Coin] *800. A Perfect Defense grants [Artifact Material Coin] *1600.
④ Members of the Guild occupying a castle will receive [Occupier Gift Box] *2 as an individual reward. Those who participate in the Guild War for at least 5 minutes will also receive [Participation Gift Box] *2.

2. Stronghold Glorious Metal Rewards
① Guilds can obtain Glorious Metal rewards by capturing offensive strongholds. Strongholds in large/medium/small castles contain 8/5/3 Glorious Metal rewards, respectively.
② Glorious Metal rewards from the same stronghold cannot be obtained more than once. A maximum of 5 Glorious Metal rewards can be obtained in each Guild War.
③ For each Glorious Metal reward obtained from a large/medium/small castle, the Guild will receive [Artifact Material Coin] *200/150/100, respectively.
④ When the attacking side obtains a Glorious Metal reward, Guild members within the stronghold can receive individual rewards, including a certain number of [Badges of Honor]. The smaller the size of the Guild’s original castle and the larger the size of the castle attacked, the greater the rewards.

3. Guild War Objectives and Settlement Rewards
While on the Guild War battlefield, tap the Details button on the right-side function bar to open the [Guild War Objectives and Settlement] interface.
① Group Objective Rewards
★ After all group objectives have been completed, each Guild member can receive [Prayer Chip Pack] *4 after the castle settlement period ends.
② Individual Objective Rewards
★ Completing individual objectives grants the corresponding objective rewards and Excellence Points.
③ Reward Bonuses
★ Members of Guilds that own medium castles receive 25% more rewards beyond the base limit when completing group and individual objectives. Members of Guilds that own small castles receive 50% more, as do members of Guilds without a castle.
★ The reward for [Base Individual Objective Honor Points for This Match] does not receive any additional bonus.
④ Guild Settlement Rewards
★ Meeting a settlement condition grants the Guild 1 random [Postwar Reconstruction Red Packet]. Each condition can grant only 1 red packet. It will be sent to the Guild Leader’s mailbox after the castle settlement period ends.
★ After a [Postwar Reconstruction Red Packet] is issued, all adventurers whose participation data appears in the Guild’s [Latest Battle Report] can claim it.

4. MVP Kill Reward
The Guild that lands the final blow on the large-castle MVP [Shadow of Morroc] will receive a certain amount of Artifact Materials.

5. Whenever rewards are calculated based on a Guild’s castle occupation status, the Guild’s status before the current Guild War began will be used.
★ For example, if a Guild did not occupy a castle when the Guild War began, its rewards will still be calculated as a [Guild Without a Castle], even if it occupies a castle during the current Guild War.

【Dungeon Overview】
After many years, the Geffen Magic Tournament is finally being held once again! This time, all aspiring contenders may participate, regardless of class or faction, as long as they possess courage and wisdom.
【Dungeon Rules】
1. Once the tournament begins, you will battle four teams in sequence. Defeating all members of an opposing team counts as victory for that round. The Tournament Committee will immediately issue the corresponding victory reward, but each account may claim this reward only once.
2. If the adventurer party is completely wiped out during battle, the challenge for that round will be considered a failure. No victory rewards or points will be awarded, and the dungeon will reset to its state before that round began.
3. During battle, the Tournament Committee will score the adventurer party based on its performance. The score is currently determined by three factors: time taken to win, total damage sustained by the party, and number of party revivals. Points are deducted for all three factors—the longer it takes to win, the more total damage the party sustains, and the more times party members are revived, the lower the final score will be.
4. Before the tournament officially begins, the party leader may speak with the host to select additional rules for the match. These include adjusting the opponents’ strength and choosing certain affix effects to enhance or restrict the actions of either side. These choices will affect the score multiplier, so party leaders should choose carefully.
5. A score will be awarded upon winning each round, and all members of the same party will receive the same score. If this score is an adventurer’s new personal best, the Tournament Committee will update their record. The final score is calculated by adding together the adventurer’s highest recorded score from each of the four battles. Scores do not affect eligibility for victory rewards.
6. Each season lasts two weeks. At the end of the season, all adventurers will be ranked according to their final scores, and ranking rewards will be distributed based on ranking percentile. Adventurers with the same final score will share the same rank and receive identical ranking rewards. Adventurers with no score will not be included in the rankings.
7. Once the first battle begins, adventurers can no longer enter the dungeon using the Follow function. Inside the dungeon, adventurers may freely switch classes before each battle begins, but cannot change classes during battle.
8. Note: For damage calculations, the Magic Tournament is treated as a PvP dungeon, and opposing teams are treated as hostile adventurers. Items prohibited in team-based competitive matches, such as Honey, are also prohibited in the Magic Tournament.

White Cat Lasgand waits for the Adventurer at Frozen Scale Bridge. The White Eagle vanguard has already infiltrated Ice Bound Castle, awaiting a coordinated attack from within and without. However, Lasgand's consciousness still has not appeared. The scattered refining experiment records by the bridge, the robe stained with blue-gold blood, and the bloodthirsty-born Frozen Grass all point to a cruel fact—Lasgand's true body has had its Mind Source stripped away by Bagg, and the refining of the imitation Yimir's Heart has entered its final stage. 
Following the blood trail and aura, the Adventurer arrives at Ice Bound Scale. Deep among the disordered experimental vessels, Lasgand's body is confined within Frozen Grass, power continuously draining from the hollow in his chest. The white cat understands that the true body is about to collapse, so it pretends to be at ease and asks the Adventurer to go under the Eternal Silence Tree to collect snowflakes and build a white cat snow sculpture modeled after itself as a farewell. In reality, after the Adventurer leaves, it has already returned to Lasgand's body, using the will it carries to steady this heartless body. 
After the Adventurer brings back the Eternal Silence Snowflake, Lasgand awakens and, when the white cat snow sculpture is completed, witnesses Snowflake Crown·Eternal Silence manifest. Eternal Silence is not an end; rather, after all sounds have vanished, it is still the choice to move forward. In its own way, the white cat places the final authority into the Adventurer's hands. After putting on the Crown of Eternal Silence, the Adventurer repels the corrupted Lugan Tribe and, together with Lasgand, heads to Ice Bound Castle to reclaim the Heart and rescue Cenia. 
In Ice Bound Castle, Lasgand's Heart has been refined into the prototype of an imitation Yimir's Heart, while Cenia is confined in an extractor, her power transformed into purple refining fire that continuously burns the Heart. Bagg declares that he is not simply seizing the Heart, but analyzing, reproducing, and surpassing Yimir's Heart. Lasgand sees through the transmission pattern of the protective wall and guides the Adventurer to break the Barrier. In direct confrontation, Lasgand, having lost his Heart, cannot suppress Bagg, so he induces Mind Source Consonance, making the Heart that still remembers him respond to the call, piercing Bagg and also scattering the refining restraints on Cenia. 
After Cenia awakens, she grieves that Lasgand failed to reclaim the Heart. But Lasgand judges that after Bagg takes away the half-finished imitation Yimir's Heart, he will certainly continue his frenzied refining; if the refining truly can be completed, it might instead become the breach in the final ending. Thus, he has the Adventurer release a signal to summon Qiyangyang, and orders the White Eagle Guard to track Bagg's whereabouts and escort the weakened Cenia to safety. 
Before the final intelligence returns, Lasgand leads the Adventurer to three pure places to find a way to stabilize the heartless body. The Wishing Snowflake sends down a blessing, keeping him conscious amid severe pain; the Ice Bound Garden condenses a Snow Heart, temporarily sustaining the flow of life; and from the Snow and Ice Paradise they retrieve the snake slough Lasgand left behind in his childhood, making him remember once more why he originally wanted to protect this land. The Heart has never been merely a beating piece of flesh; innocence, faith, and the desire to protect can likewise keep a heartless body moving forward. 
After Qiyangyang brings back the intelligence, the Adventurer and Lasgand step into the Ice Bound Heart. Bagg first tests everyone with ice-forged specimens, then takes action personally, and finally uses the half-finished imitation Yimir's Heart to transform into a gigantic mutated Bagg, declaring that he will use himself as the refining vessel so that the divine power mortals look up to can complete its cycle within his body. In the final battle, the mutated Bagg completes the final refining, but is also annihilated under the combined attack of the Adventurer and Lasgand. The completed imitation Yimir's Heart floats in the air; Lasgand does not let it return to his chest, but instead lets it transform into the first snow belonging to Isgard. 
The imitation Yimir's Heart transforms into snowflakes filling the sky and falls to the earth, purifying the corrupted Lugan Tribe, ending this nightmare, and also allowing the white cat to return from the snow at Ice Bound Scale. Originally, when the Heart returned to heaven and earth, Lasgand's heartless body should also have dissipated; but Isgard responded to the one willing to return everything to the land. Golden light surging from the earth envelops Lasgand, and with his heartless body he continues to stand in the first snow, opening a new chapter belonging to himself, the Lugan Tribe, and Isgard. 
Oscar descends and confirms that the page in the Book of Fate with the most questions has finally found its answer. When the Wind of Fate blows once more, a familiar voice comes through the first snow: "We agreed to walk through every corner of the world together... Do you still remember?"
